News.title: Cops turning on Burnham will be a big blow to the PM… He needs to be on THEIR side, not that of smirking killers
News.content:
WHEN Andy Burnham announced last year that Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson was to remain at the head of Greater Manchester Police for a ­further two years, he did so with considerable pride.

Watson, he said, had delivered a ­“colossal turnaround” in the UK’s second- largest police force, making “significant strides” to ensure the city’s streets ­were safer, adding: “We are backing him to ­finish the job.”



There is no question that Watson is a real coppers’ copper who oversaw important changes in Manchester.

And that is why his signature on a letter from 50 police chiefs calling for the Prime Minister to block the release of two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers will have been a significant, and very painful, blow.



But this loss of confidence from Britain’s top cops has not happened overnight.

First there was the reaction of Thames Valley Police Chief Constable Jason Hogg, who said in August he was “beyond ­disappointed” that smirking killers Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole would be eligible for early release.



On Monday, he was joined by Thames Valley Police and Crime Commissioner, Matthew Barber, and Chair of the Thames Valley Police Federation, Aileen O’Connor, who wrote to Burnham urging him to keep the pair behind bars.

Their words show these police leaders understand the psychological impact of this debate on frontline officers.

They will have had conversations with them, which I can imagine — and I’m sure your readers can too — beginning with the words: “Boss, they don’t have our backs.”

Policing is on its knees, and those at the top understand that our officers need to feel the Government has their backs when they run towards danger — as PC Harper did.



The senior policing community do not always acquit themselves well when ­dealing with the state.

However, I believe their open letter today is driven by a genuine sense of ­outrage that politicians could be so callous as to forget the impact of the chaotic early release scheme on their officers.

This is Burnham’s first test as Prime Minister, and maybe he will learn from it.

Maybe he will learn that the Ministry of Justice is full of people who are wildly incompetent and have made careers out of failing upwards.



In their advice to him in this case, they have failed spectacularly.

The party line is that the exemption of PC Harper’s killers is impossible.

Yet no one has explained why it would be impossible to pass primary legislation to exempt those convicted of the ­manslaughter of police officers.

Similar legislation has been created to detain ­terrorists in the past.



Are we saying that the apparatus of the state is unable to fix this problem?

Rather than listening to advisers who are trying to protect their reputations, ­Burnham should be listening to the police officers who have been left demoralised.

He should be listening to PC Harper’s family, and thousands of other victims who are faced with the agony of not knowing whether or not the perpetrators of crimes against them will soon be back walking the streets.

And yet this is not the first time a ­failure to tackle prison system issues has derailed a Prime Minister in the early days of their premiership.

Just two months after he was sworn in in July 2024, Keir Starmer saw criminals popping champagne corks outside ­Wandsworth Prison as they celebrated their early release under his scheme to ease prison overcrowding.



The embarrassing episode came when the new PM was still finding his feet, and some would say he never recovered from it.

Which begs the question: When will politicians learn that draining confidence in the prison system is electoral ­kryptonite?

Clearly Burnham is not a ­student of recent history.



His response may be that Labour ­inherited this mess from the ­Conservative government, and that they have “no choice” but to act as our prisons are fast approaching full capacity.

While I suspect the Ministry of Justice projections may overestimate the speed at which this is happening, we do of course have an urgent problem with prison ­overcrowding in this country.

In my view, the only way to deal with this is with the rapid expansion of the prison estate — which is possible, if not ­palatable.

In recent years, statistics show the ­number of female inmates is down. Releasing 40 per cent of these — ­excluding those in for violent and/or sexual offences — would free up hundreds of spaces.

Removing non-violent criminals who have offended due to drug addiction to secure NHS detox facilities could free up as many as 5,000 places.



Existing prisons which have been closed down, such as HMP Dartmoor and HMP Camp Hill, could also be used to create headroom.

The helpless inability to ­mobilise the enormous resources of the state to create additional space is woeful.

And there are further options which could be explored.

In 1997, the Labour government introduced HMP Weare — a ship moored in Portland Harbour — to ease overcrowding.

Before its closure in 2005, it held 400 inmates who consistently said the ­conditions on board were better than in prisons like Brixton.



There are no easy options here.

But if Burnham is to survive this first test, he needs to stop listening to the usual suspects in the prison reform ­system who were responsible for telling him that keeping Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole in prison was “impossible”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Instead, he needs to start listening to the public — who have, to date, left almost a ­million signatures on a petition for the killers to remain caged.

And he needs to listen to the frontline police officers who leave home each ­morning knowing that — like PC Harper — they may not come back.­

News.title: Andy Burnham should stop lecturing Brits on illegal migrants and actually come up with plan to stop mega-dinghies
News.content:
Stop the boasts

ANDY Burnham’s reaction to public fury at illegal migrants being housed in their communities spoke volumes.

“I believe all parts of the country need to work, to play their part,” he said.



His suggestion that every area must accommodate asylum seekers who leave France entirely misses the point.

It’s not a question of families playing their part.



Those tens of thousands of incomers — many of them young men, some of whom will pose a public danger — should NOT be here in the first place.

Burnham’s astonishingly tin-eared plea came just hours after Angela Rayner wrongly suggested most migrants were vulnerable women and children. They just don’t get it.



An illegal migrant is currently landing on our shores EVERY 14 MINUTES.

Instead of lecturing the public on their responsibilities, how about Burnham gets round to holding an emergency Cobra meeting on the mega-dinghies?

All we’ve had so far is ministers boasting about cutting the number of asylum hotels when they are dumping migrants in Houses of Multiple Occupation.

Or the Government claiming to have cut crossings by 40 per cent when it’s widely acknowledged that the weather remains the only reliable way of stopping the boats.



Where is the Rwanda-style deterrent that was showing signs it could work before Labour foolishly axed it? Where is the action on ending free housing and benefits for asylum seekers?

What, Prime Minister, is the plan?

In a right state

KEIR Starmer once bemoaned the Civil Service for sitting in the tepid bath of managed decline.

It seems under a new Prime Minister that the temperature has dropped another few degrees.

Whitehall’s response to prison overcrowding has been inept.



Their “can’t do” attitude has forced a disastrous early release scheme that the Chief Inspector of Prisons says could inflict a wave of rape and murder.

Is it any wonder we see so much state uselessness when the majority of civil servants can swap working at their desks for sitting at home in the sunshine?

Keep it down

CHANCELLOR John Healey says his ­number one mission is to ease the cost of living for families.

There is one surefire way to do just that: Scrap the 5p fuel duty increase due to kick in on January 1.

So far, Andy Burnham has been happy to spend billions to knock £45 off energy bills or a quid off bus fares.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Keeping pump prices down would put a bit more money back in the family coffers and help to rein in food prices.

That’s how to make a REAL difference.

News.title: Tate brothers’ multiple passports under bizarre aliases are unearthed – including Bond villain
News.content:
ALLEGED rapists Andrew and Tristan Tate had held several passports under different aliases – including one name borrowed from a Bond villain.

Court documents show Tristan Tate held a Mexican passport with his photo and date of birth, but a mysterious different name.



The passport was under the name “Vladimir Scorpius” – the eponymous villain of the 007 spy novel “Scorpius”, court documents show.

Tristan also posted an online video declaring “I’m Vladimir Scorpius” and registered a UK company called “Scorpius Ltd.” in reference to the fictional arms dealer from the 1988 novel by John Gardner.



Meanwhile, Andrew Tate openly bragged on social media about having “8 lives … 8 licenses and passports,” and evading authorities in multiple countries, according to the documents.

Prosecutors also claim Andrew was in possession of a stash of travel documents from the UK, US, Estonia, Nigeria, Poland and the Pacific island nation of Vanuatu.

The shocking details about the manosphere influencers‘ series of identities were revealed in new filings from the British Embassy in Washington this week in the Southern District of Florida.

The embassy is currently fighting the brothers’ bid to be released on bond as they seek to avoid extradition to the UK.



The filing warns they pose a flight risk, citing dozens of post by Andrew that “demonstrate that he has access to multiple passports, and that he is willing to use false identities to evade law enforcement”.

In one video, Andrew claimed if he was stopped by police, he would simply “pull out a licence from some random country” to hide his real identity.

British prosecutors also allege there is “substantial grounds to believe that Andrew Tate and Tristan Tate would attempt to identify and interfere with witnesses if released”.

Andrew Tate, 39, and his brother Tristan, 38, were arrested at a bare-knuckle boxing event in Miami on July 18.

They are currently being held in secure housing in federal detention.



Andrew described his Special Housing Unit (SHU) as “punitive housing for people who murder their cellmates“.

He also claimed he was staying in “the worst possible conditions the US gov provides to terrorists and psychopaths”, before adding the inmate in the neighbouring cell was a “cannibal who screams throughout the night”.

His only water source, he complains, is a shower and a “brown and filthy faucet” which has left him suffering “persistent stomach problems”.

In another message on X, Andrew woefully claimed he had “no commissary. No visits. No contact with the outside world.”

“I am an innocent until proven guilty extradition detainee. I’m wanted by a foreign state. I am an American citizen. WHY AM I HERE?” he demanded.



The brothers are fighting extradition to the UK, where they face a total of 59 criminal charges, including rape, sex trafficking and offenses related to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

A detention hearing has been scheduled for Thursday.

British prosecutors say these latest charges were fast-tracked after authorities investigated claims made by another four victims.

These new claims are part of a long-running international legal battle involving the Tates, spaning across the US, Britain and Romania.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The pair are being criminally prosecuted over allegations which include having sex with a minor, trafficking minors, running an organised crime operation and money laundering.



Andrew and Tristan have denied all charges against them.

News.title: One illegal immigrant has landed on British shores every FOURTEEN minutes since Labour took power, shock figures show
News.content:
ONE illegal immigrant every 14 minutes has landed in Britain since Labour took power, figures show.

More than 80,000 have crossed the Channel in the 768 days since the party made it into Number 10 in July, 2024.



Since Andy Burnham took over the tiller as PM, 3,000 have arrived — 230 of them on a mega-dinghy dragged into Dover on Monday.

Mr Burnham has vowed to “change our tactics” to tackle the smuggling gangs but has not given a timeline for stopping the crossings.



The Tories, however, insist Britain must leave the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR) so arrivals cannot challenge their deportations.

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “Open-borders Burnham has offered nothing but platitudes.

“He’s given zero indication he will do anything differently to Sir Keir Starmer’s failed record on tackling illegal immigration.

“Labour will never take the action needed to face down this crisis, because ending it would mean leaving the ECHR.

“We will leave the ECHR, ban asylum claims from illegal entrants and deport illegal immigrants rapidly.”

Mr Burnham’s stop the crossings vow comes despite the failures by former PMs Sir Keir, Rishi Sunak and Boris Johnson. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage told The Sun: “They tell the public what they want to hear.



“None of them have got the balls to actually deal with this. And I tell you what, I have.”

A Government spokesman said last night: “We’re cracking down on these reckless and dangerous gangs.

“Small boat crossings are significantly down this year.”

Home Office minister Anna Turley, meanwhile, has defended Labour’s plans to house asylum seekers in old military bases in the countryside.

News.title: Britain’s top cop says justice has not been served in PC Harper case as he pays tribute to 3 officers murdered in 1966
News.content:
BRITAIN’S top cop paid tribute yesterday to three police officers murdered in cold blood in 1966 — then said the justice meted out to their killers was not served in the case of PC Andrew Harper.

Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said the victims of an armed robbery gang 60 years ago had died in a “routine moment”, just like Thames Valley officer Andrew who was dragged to his death in 2018.



But while the 1966 killers had been locked up for a total of 108 years, he said the trust that existed back then in the criminal justice system to do the right thing had been “badly damaged” today.

He said: “The State, whose first duty is to protect its citizens, must today remember how to nourish routine policing courage, not to treat it with cavalier disregard.”



Sir Mark was speaking at a 60th anniversary service at the scene in Shepherd’s Bush, West London, where DS Christopher Head, 30, DC David Wombwell, 25, and PC Geoffrey Fox, 41, were shot dead.

The officers, in a Triumph 2000 patrol car, were murdered after pulling over the gang’s motor.



Leader Harry Roberts served 48 years in prison and died last December aged 89.

His accomplices John Duddy and John Witney each got at least 30 years. Duddy died in prison in 1981 aged 52. Witney was 69 when beaten to death by his flatmate in 1991, eight years after his release.



PC Harper, 28, died in 2019 after being dragged for more than a mile by a getaway car used in a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berks.

Sir Mark is one of 50 police chiefs to sign an open letter to PM Andy Burnham urging him to pursue “every legal option” to stop the early release of Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, two of newly-married PC Harper’s three killers.

He said: “The case of PC Andrew Harper has left officers across the country angry and upset that the family of a former colleague who lost his life protecting others should be treated so poorly.



“It has also left them seriously doubting, in their own routine moments of personal jeopardy, whether they can rely upon such whole-hearted support.”

He paid tribute to officers who risk their lives to protect communities, and added: “That is the golden thread that connects today’s officers to Christopher, David and Geoffrey.”

Sir Mark, the 1966 victims’ loved ones and policing organisations laid wreaths at a memorial stone at the spot where the officers were killed.

Following yesterday’s service, Sir Mark presented Elizabeth Emblem medals to their families.

The medals, introduced by King Charles, are for the next of kin of public servants who die in the line of duty. They are inscribed: “For a life given in service.”



After his speech, Sir Mark told The Sun it was “good news” PM Burnham said he aimed to stop the early release of Cole and Bowers, who got 13 years each for manslaughter, under changes introduced by the Sentencing Act.

News.title: ‘Love rat’ Scots minister suspended by Kirk after wife accuses him of affair in front of packed church service
News.content:
IT'S A SIN ‘Love rat’ Scots minister suspended by Kirk after wife accuses him of affair in front of packed church service

A MINISTER accused by his wife during a service of having an affair with a parishioner has been suspended.

Kirk bosses said Rev Edward Lyons, 48, now faces a misconduct probe.



We told how his missus Caroline, 45, made the claim as he was giving a sermon at Penninghame St John’s Parish Church in Newton Stewart, Wigtownshire.

A spokesman for the Church of Scotland confirmed: “Rev Lyons has been administratively suspended from his role and is subject to disciplinary proceedings under Church law.



“It would be inappropriate to make any further comment.”

He wouldn’t say whether Rev Lyons conducted a service on Sunday before his suspension.

Read more Scottish news SIN OF A PREACHER MAN Cheating Reverend's affair exposed by wife at packed church service



We also revealed Caroline took to social media after the incident to ask where she could find packing boxes.

Her hubby was then seen loading a bike and other belongings into a car outside the manse he shared with his spouse of 22 years.



Later the motor was parked at a nearby pad understood to be the other woman’s home.

Locals told how she and Rev Lyons were spotted together at a supermarket.

We previously told how the claims about the “trendy” clergyman, who is a karate blackbelt, have stunned the congregation at his church.

A source told The Scottish Sun on Sunday: “Everybody is talking about it. Edward was very popular and highly thought of so these allegations have come as a complete and utter shock.

“He’s just the stereotypical trendy young minister.



“He has longer hair, a beard, he plays electric guitar, does karate and rides a bike. His wife said he had been cheating on her with a senior member of the flock and it looks like she has booted him out.

“Edward appears to be staying with the new woman and they’ve been seen down at the supermarket. He preaches family values and thou shalt not commit adultery but it seems he might be a total hypocrite.”

Lyons, from Drumchapel, Glasgow, was said to be an atheist during his younger years as a biochemistry student at Strathclyde University.

But he switched paths after attending a Christmas Eve church service and was ordained two decades ago. He landed his first role in Stirling.

He and Caroline met during a youth mission week.



It is believed she revealed fears just days after their anniversary that he had strayed with a long-time parishioner who has been involved in events at the kirk.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Lyons was seen in a T-shirt and jeans as he left the home provided by the church.

Officials admitted it was a “difficult time for all those involved”.

News.title: How ‘Mindhunter’ who claimed to have quizzed world’s worst killers was fantasist PC from Kettering exposed by The Sun
News.content:
KILLER CON How ‘Mindhunter’ who claimed to have quizzed world’s worst killers was fantasist PC from Kettering exposed by The Sun

AS a criminal profiler dubbed Britain’s Mindhunter, Paul Harrison had his audience entranced with chilling tales of the world’s most notorious serial killers.

A packed theatre sat spellbound as he recounted his ­meetings with Jeffrey Dahmer, Ted Bundy and John Wayne Gacy in a bid to work out what made them tick — and all at the request of the FBI.



The only problem was, none of it was true.

Harrison, also a true crime author, made an estimated £100,000 from sell-out shows like the one I attended at the Tyne Theatre in Newcastle.



But that event would prove to be the beginning of his end after I set about investigating his fantastical claims to have quizzed 70 of the world’s worst killers.

When The Sun published an exposé in 2019 — revealing that in reality Harrison had been a beat bobby in Kettering, Northants — he apologised to fans and vanished from public view.

But his incredible story is now being retold in an absorbing ­podcast called The Mindhunter.

Narrated by journalist Francisco Garcia, the six-part Audible Original show, out today, lays bare the full extent of Harrison’s deception.

As well as his criminal profiling claims, he also said he had been at gangster Reggie Kray’s death bed, had worked as a close personal protection officer for the King of Jordan and was the inspiration for numerous fictional television detectives.

He also reckons he worked as a firearms officer escorting nuclear convoys and as an undercover officer who had infiltrated a football hooligan gang.



In an earlier and even more bizarre chapter of his life, he even faked his own death amid a legal battle, claiming to have died on an archaeological dig in Egypt.

The case has striking parallels to that of Professor Jason Arday, the academic who last week quit Cambridge University over a string of dodgy claims about his achievements.

Fantasist Harrison targeted the world of true crime rather than academia but, just like Arday, his sparkling CV went unchallenged for years.



Following his supposed death in Egypt, he re-emerged a few years later, claiming to be one of the world’s foremost experts on criminal psychology.

Harrison alleged that he first worked with the FBI in 1982 when agents invited him to its Quantico academy after he wrote to them out of the blue about his interest in profiling.

He said he was given access to America’s most infamous killers on an almost daily basis and worked on and off with the FBI for a decade.

As well as Dahmer, Bundy and Gacy, he said he had met Charles Manson and Amityville Horror murderer Ronald DeFeo.

Harrison told his audiences: “Ted Bundy walked in like Liam Gallagher. He had a look of contempt on his face. He slowly walked behind me and stopped right behind me.



“Every part of my body was telling me to look round as you’ve got Ted Bundy behind you. I sensed him move forward, I felt his body heat on me. Then he bent down.

“He sniffed me and I thought this is going to be horrific, but he said, ‘I can smell your cologne’.”

In his book Mind Games, Harrison boasted that Bundy told him he was the “guy who gets inside our heads”.

He said he worked with the FBI’s pioneering Behavioural Science Unit which features in the film Silence Of The Lambs and the Netflix series Mindhunter, leading to his nickname of Britain’s Mindhunter.



Harrison’s growing profile meant he landed a regular slot on the CBS Reality channel as a criminal expert and was able to splash out on a ­Jaguar, which he drove to his shows.

He also claimed that Peter Sutcliffe invited him to Broadmoor so they could discuss writing his life story — but that they failed to hit it off.

Harrison said in an interview: “He said to me, ‘Why are you so cold towards me? You seem completely indifferent to me. I’m scared of you’.

“I wanted to tell him what I thought. I said to him, ‘Good. I don’t like you’.”



Harrison also claimed that notorious London gangster Reggie Kray wanted him to write his life story, and that they became such close pals he invited him to visit him on his deathbed in 2000.

But his barely believable claims — and his lucrative career — fell apart when The Sun began investigating.

It is not easy to prove someone did not do something they claimed they did, especially when it was decades ago in the pre-internet age.

I knew that the only way we could publicly accuse Harrison of being a fantasist was to methodically unpick every one of his claims.

I had a contact who had links to the Krays’ inner circle who was able to check for me whether he had indeed been a friend of Reggie’s.



Former Krays henchman Freddie Foreman responded with the message: “Reggie Kray was not a friend of Paul Harrison. He wouldn’t entertain the police in his company and he certainly wasn’t at Reggie’s final days.”

Another contact was close to the Yorkshire Ripper and was able to ask Sutcliffe whether he had ever invited Harrison to Broadmoor.

His response, in a letter passed to The Sun before his death in 2020, was even more cutting, calling Harrison a “charlatan, a con man and a wazzock”.



He added: “He never corresponded with me, nor did he ever visit me.”

Crucially, I needed to check ­Harrison’s claims that he had worked for the FBI.

The agency’s press office would not help with staffing matters so I tracked down former agent Mark Safarik, who did work in the Behavioural Science Unit for 12 years.

He told me: “I have never heard of Paul Harrison. He is making all this up.”

Not only that, Mark reached out to a number of other former agents, seven of whom confirmed they had never heard of Harrison.



The most bizarre chapter of Harrison’s life came in 2010 when he sued Carlisle United over the copyright of some photos the club had used. As well as being a Leeds fan, Harrison is a Carlisle supporter and has written a number of books about the club.

But he had a falling-out with them over the snaps and took the club to court in a case which would have left him with a hefty legal bill had he lost. It was lined up to be heard at Romford County Court in London but the court then received a letter to say Harrison was dead.

Fellow Carlisle fan Neil Nixon heard the news and wrote an obituary in a fanzine, but was then stunned to discover Harrison was still alive.

Neil said: “He sent me an email to tell me he’d been through some really difficult stuff. I was left thoroughly bemused.”

Harrison has been married four times, with his third marriage to Mandy Doyle falling apart after we published our investigation.



Mandy said: “When he started the serial killer talks he got bigger and bigger. It was amazing and the money he made was ridiculous. He would come home with wads of cash.

“I think he made around £100,000, easily, but his books were all fiction.

“I did the research on the killers for him. He never met any of them.” When he was exposed, Harrison posted on Facebook to say: “I’ve let everyone down, I’m sorry.”

He has never responded to The Sun’s requests for comment and did not respond this time either.

But he did send an email to the podcast team answering some of the claims against him.



However, he did not respond to the claims that he was never a criminal profiler, had never spoken to Peter Sutcliffe and was not present in Reggie Kray’s final days.

In relation to the stories told in his show, he said: “I won’t discuss in depth the shows. I was always told they were good entertainment.

“The producers knew and were told they were for entertainment purposes.”

He denied writing the Facebook message apologising to fans, blaming it on his social media team. He did not deny an email was sent to people saying he had died, but did deny that he sent it.

He maintains that he did work as a protection officer for the King of Jordan, as a nuclear cop and as an undercover cop and that he had been the inspiration for TV detectives.



He described the claims that he made up his meetings with notorious serial killers as “false allegations” and said they would be dealt with in his own podcast in the near future.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Until then, fans of true crime — and all the other areas Harrison has written books about — can tune in to The Mindhunter to decide for themselves whether his incredible life is fact or fiction.

News.title: Labour MP accused of raiding historic cafe’s fridges during sombre D-Day trip after fellow backbencher missed ferry
News.content:
WORLD WAR BRIE Labour MP accused of raiding historic cafe’s fridges during sombre D-Day trip after fellow backbencher missed ferry

A LABOUR MP has been accused of raiding a historic cafe’s fridge on a sombre trip to Normandy to mark the anniversary of D-Day.

Amanda Martin is said to have barged into the kitchen and started helping herself to food at the Café Gondrée, the first place liberated by the Allies during the landings in 1944.



The visit last June caused further embarrassment when fellow backbencher Samantha Niblett reportedly missed the ferry over to France, then clashed with the organisers.

Both of them were later ticked off by Commons Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle.



A source told The Sun: “It was quite embarassing, really.”

Both MPs are understood to believe the episodes are “misunderstandings” and insist they did not misbehave.

They are also understood to deny being reprimanded by Sir Lindsay and instead said they discussed the “misunderstandings”.

The Speaker’s Office declined to comment.

A Labour spokesperson said: “Both MPs were honoured to visit France with the Armed Forces Parliamentary Scheme, which provides valuable insight into military life and the brave work our servicemen and women do to keep Britain safe.”

News.title: 'Nigel Farage’s £250,000 Clacton by-election stunt cannot make the investigation disappear'
News.content:
'Nigel Farage’s £250,000 Clacton by-election stunt cannot make the investigation disappear'

"For a man who has built a career denouncing waste in Westminster and Whitehall, the contradiction is glaring, with the cost of polling stations, staff, security and a count of ballot papers"

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Nigel Farage has for years won support by selling himself as the taxpayer’s watchdog, hunting down waste and making Westminster answer for every penny.

On Thursday, that collides with reality as the people of Clacton go back to the polls in a by-election costing around £250,000 of vital public money, despite electing him as their MP only two years ago. There was no death, no boundary change, no scandal serious enough to force him out. Just Farage’s decision to resign.

Farage has always understood the power of the outsider, the man who says ­that ­politicians live by one set of rules while ordinary people live by another. But accountability has to apply when the scrutiny lands on you.

The Reform UK leader walked away while Parliament’s standards watchdog was investigating his failure to declare a £5million gift from Thai cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne. His explanation for that money has shifted more than once: security costs, a reward for Brexit, then simply cash he was free to spend as he pleased.

Farage denies wrongdoing, and no finding has been made against him so far. Those facts matter.

Article continues below

So does another: when Farage stopped being an MP, the investigation stopped with him. If he returns to ­Parliament, it can begin again.

That is what makes this election so hard to justify. Farage could have remained representing the people who elected him, and let the process reach its conclusion.

For a man who has built a career denouncing waste in Westminster and Whitehall, the contradiction is glaring. There’s the cost of polling stations, staff, security and a count of ballot papers with a record 34 candidates.

Article continues below

We already know the script if Farage wins: Clacton has spoken, the establishment has been defeated, Reform is unstoppable. The trouble is, none of the major parties have fielded a candidate.

Farage may win handsomely, but one needless by-election does not prove the country has embraced him as its next Prime Minister.

This is bigger than Count Binface, a giant ballot paper or the circus gathered around this election. It is about the standards we demand from people who seek power.

News.title: Solar eclipse watchers rejoice as Moon slides in front of Sun for once-in-a-lifetime celestial display
News.content:
Thousands of people across the UK and Europe were left in awe today after the continent's first total solar eclipse in nearly three decades blotted out the sun and doused searing temperatures.

Crowds fell silent across the country and beyond, including in Land's End, the UK's most southerly point, this evening as the moon moved in front of the sun, switching a bright evening to near-complete nighttime for just over a minute. Locals were treated to some of the best views in the country as 98.5 percent of the sun was covered by the earth's natural satellite.

Hundreds excitedly gathered on a cliff top overlooking the Channel and Celtic sea ahead of the phenomenon, while millions of others across Spain, France and other nations in western Europe were treated to even more dramatic displays.

View 17 Images Spain was lucky enough to capture the glow of a full ring around the moon (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Many people had travelled from far and wide to catch a glimpse of the first eclipse, which is set to be the last on British shores for another nearly 70 years. Susan Carpenter, 70, was among them. She drove down to Cornwall from Newbury, Berkshire, on Wednesday morning with her husband, daughter and grandson. She told the Mirror: “For the last eclipse in 1999, we took our children to Devon and we’ve brought our grandson so he can experience an eclipse. The last one [eclipse] was phenomenal —it was at 11 in the morning."

View 17 Images Susan Carpenter

“Everything went black and the birds went to sleep and as it went over the birds started to wake and you get the dawn chorus. The children couldn’t believe it. It’s a really good experience.” Steve Lipscombe, from Mitcham, South London, watched the 1999 eclipse from Devon, but last minute cloud cover obscured his view.

He said: “I was in Penzance with the Radio 1 roadshow they did back then. It was a lovely day like today, but it went cloudy just as the eclipse was starting to happen, so we basically missed it, which was terrible — I’d travelled 300 miles there and back, so I’m back again today for take two."

‌



View 17 Images Reporter Saskia got one of the last pairs of eclipse glasses (Image: Saskia Rowlands)

“I like celestial things, I’ve seen many shooting star showers - but there’s not another eclipse for 65 years in this country.”

Shop Judy’s Body Art, a shack next to the infamous Land’s End sign, had sold more than 140 pairs of eclipse glasses in just two hours. Owner Judith Dyulaine Buskas, who sold our reporter one of her last pairs, said: “We have been very busy today, and only have a few pairs left."

View 17 Images Spain was rewarded with some of the best views on Wednesday (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



“We are very excited for tonight - it will be the last eclipse in my lifetime.” The atmosphere was just as palpable in western Europe, with beaches in northern France, one of the best viewing points on the continent, crammed with both locals and holidaymakers.

On the Baie de Somme hundreds sat enjoying picnics as the eclipse edged nearer. In the Picardy village of Le Crotoy people took to the huge beach for the best view.

View 17 Images Onlookers were overjoyed by the incredible display (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Northern Spain and Iceland were among the nations that received a totality this evening - meaning the moon covered nearly 100 percent of the sun's surface. The display was received by whoops and cheers in Reykjavic, Iceland's caputal, and in Burgos, Spain, with some people left dumbstruck.

‌



Dhara Patel, who is a space expert at the National Space Centre, said some people may be overcome by emotion while watching the eclipse.

View 17 Images A passenger plane flies in front of the solar eclipse near Heathrow (Image: / SWNS)

Speaking at the UK’s largest space attraction in Leicester, she said: “For a lot of people, it can be a little bit of an emotional event. I’ve seen previously people being drawn to tears or just have a really good moment within themselves where they realise they’re seeing or witnessing something… you’ve never seen before in your life."

She described it as “incredible” to be able to witness this eclipse, adding: “We’ve had solar eclipses over the last couple of years, about 30% coverage."

‌



View 17 Images People across the UK gathered to watch the sun disappear behind the moon (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

“They’ve been good, but this is definitely a different scale. And what’s really nice is it’s a way for lots of people to come together and connect with nature – looking up at the sky at objects that we typically tend to take for granted.”

The display left onlookers literally starstruck, including 12-year-old Benjamin Firmager-Lee, who wants to work for Nasa when he is older. He was one of nearly 400 people who gathered at the National Space Centre, a planetarium in Leicester, to see the eclipse during a special event.

View 17 Images The eclipse behind Torrespana TV tower in Madrid (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



He said: “It’s like a once in a lifetime thing to see, so it was quite exciting to see how it changed over time. It’s really quite rare so it’s quite cool to see. Looking through all the telescopes was really interesting to see how it changed position over time.”

He added: “I do like learning about stuff like space.” The crowd of people erupted into cheers after counting down from 10 until the eclipse reached its maximum coverage.

View 17 Images A total solar eclipse as seen from Valencia, Spain (Image: Getty Images)

Will O’Grady, 36, who is studying physics at Cardiff University, brought a telescope to Cardiff Bay and shared it with dozens of people passing by. The masters student said: “Loads of kids loved it. It’s nice for people who are clearly visiting from another country as well, their English is not great, but you get the idea of ‘have a look’.

‌



"The community, for two hours everyone gets together and does the same thing, I think is really quite nice. It doesn’t matter whether or not you’re really into it, whether you know anything about it, or whether you’re a geek like me. That’s what I love about things like this.”

View 17 Images Today's solar eclipse near Bury (Image: David Higgerson)

Abdul Othman, 28, who only found out about the solar eclipse event at the National Space Centre a few hours before it began, described it as “surreal”. Speaking after queuing at the venue for one of the last two tickets, he said: “It’s a once in a lifetime opportunity.

“You hear about it all the time in your life, and then to see it with your own eyes and actually see the moon go across the sky and turning the sun into just a little crescent, it’s kind of surreal."

‌



View 17 Images The solar eclipse above Croke Park, Dublin

“And then when you see the sky getting darker, that’s also quite amazing to see.” Mr Othman said he has never seen anything “on this scale” before, adding: “I can understand why people are into it now, how people make so many sacrifices just to see (it) once in a lifetime.”

In Greenwich Park, southeast London, the home of Greenwich Mean Time and the Greenwich Observatory, hundreds of people gathered.

View 17 Images Arsenal fans watch the solar eclipse ahead of the pre-season friendly match between Arsenal FC and Como Calcio (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

‌



Kim Rebecca, 26, of Canada Water, south east London, said “you could definitely notice it getting darker”. The city asset management worker added: “I have never seen an eclipse before and it is an amazing phenomenon. It is still hot but it is noticeably cooler than it was.

“You would normally think it would be quieter when it happened but, maybe because it is south east London, there was champagne corks popping."

“It has also been good because it has been a real community thing and got a lot of people together.”

View 17 Images People gathering to watch the solar eclipse in Scotland (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

‌



Van Sabellina, 31, from Truro, watched the eclipse with her husband and their baby. She said: “It was amazing — it’s a once in a lifetime. We were very lucky with the weather and being able to witness it in Land’s End was just spectacular.

“It was a bit eerie - you feel the change in temperature from hot to refreshing and cold. I feel very lucky to have watched it in this life of mine - we don’t know when there will be another one.”

View 17 Images People try out their solar eclipse glasses in Falmouth (Image: Getty Images)

Plenty of people weren't quite as fortunate, however, as cloud cover prevented them from being able to enjoy the full majesty of the eclipse on the day. Una Eggertsdóttir in Hafnarfjörður, a community 15 minutes outside of Iceland's capital Reykjavik, said it was "extremelt grey" before the eclipse materialised.

‌



She told the BBC: "It is extremely grey, cloudy and rainy so we’re not seeing much yet, and it's supposed to just get worse".

View 17 Images People watching the eclipse at Devils Dyke, East Sussex (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

She added the heartbreaking conditions were a far cry from those of just two days earlier, which would have perfectly staged the event. She said: "But our expectations were realistic. No one was expecting clear skies, but people are still excited for what happens later."

While it was Iceland, Spain, France and their neighbours all being treated to the total solar eclipse, a partial eclipse - where a smaller portion of the sun was covered by the moon - was seen across other continents.

‌



View 17 Images Solar eclipse at Devils Dyke, East Sussex

Hundreds of millions more people watched the sun being partially covered from North America, including in Alaska and Siberia. Canadians also got a glimpse of the eclipse, as were residents of parts of West and northern Africa, including in the nations of Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia.

News.title: Karoline Leavitt quits as White House Press Secretary as Trump reveals new role
News.content:
Karoline Leavitt quits as White House Press Secretary as Trump reveals new role

Donald Trump announced the departure of his press secretary on Wednesday in a post on Truth Social

View Image Donald Trump and Karoline Leavitt (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, youngest person to hold the role, will leave at month's end, Donald Trump has announced.

‌



Announcing the news on Truth Social, Trump said: "Our wonderful White House Press Secretary, and one of my most trusted aides, Karoline Leavitt, will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family, a decision I totally understand and respect!

‌



"Karoline will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party, as we work to defy History, and conclusively win the Midterm Elections."

‌



Leavitt just recently returned to the White House after taking a brief leave for the birth of her second child in May. She also has a two-year-old son.

The 28-year-old, who served Trump as a press aide during his first period in the White House, has been one of the most visible advocates of the president’s “Make America Great Again” movement, and was elevated to the role of press secretary during his second term.

‌



In a post on X, the departing press secretary said: "Being a mother and welcoming a new baby while working in one of the most demanding jobs in the world has been the most rewarding yet challenging season of my life, to say the least.

"The truth is since returning to the White House after the birth of my daughter, I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary — and that is why I have ultimately made the bittersweet decision to depart the White House and embark on a new chapter in my life."

She added: "President Trump has asked me to continue serving as a top advisor to him on the outside, and I will always remain a vocal advocate for MAGA and the Republican Party."

‌



When Leavitt's first child was born in July 2024, she took just four days of maternity leave before returning to Trump's side as she joined him on the campaign trail a day after the then-candidate was the victim on an assassination plot in Pennsylvania.

“It kind of threw me right back to work much sooner than I would have probably expected or hoped,” Leavitt later told journalist Megyn Kelly in an interview.

Yet despite acknowledging the difficulties of balancing the role with raising two small children, Leavitt said at the time that “I view this as more than job — I view this as public service.”

Article continues below

Donald Trump has not yet indicated who might who might replace her in the high-profile role, but the shakeup comes just months after two of Leavitt's communications deputies, Harrison Fields and Abigail Jackson, have also left their roles.

News.title: 'Dozens of women come forward' to police over serial sex attacker Simon Levy
News.content:
'Dozens of women come forward' to police over serial sex attacker Simon Levy

EXCLUSIVE: The Metropolitan Police is understood to be considering forming a special team to deal with a flood of reports following previous errors that left Levy free to kill

View 5 Images Simon Levy in the dock on Wednesday (Image: Julia Quenzler / SWNS)

Dozens of women have come forward to say they may been targeted by serial sex attacker Simon Levy, a source has revealed.

‌



The Metropolitan Police is understood to be thinking about forming a special team to deal with the flood of reports in an effort to avoid any further failings in investigating the double killer. It comes after a series of disastrous decisions previously left Levy free kill and assault women.

‌



The predator was given a rare whole-life order on Wednesday at the Old Bailey, meaning he will never be released. Levy, 40, was last week found guilty of smothering grandmother Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53, in March last year and mum-of-four Sheryl Wilkins, 39, five months later.

‌



He was also convicted of raping another woman and leaving her for dead in January 2025 in the same north London car park where Sheryl’s body was later found. Levy was convicted following a trial earlier this year of attacking 10 women on public transport in London, seeking out busy carriages to assault women aged between 18 and 32.

Killer Simon Levy used bus driver's stolen travelcard to move around London after police repeatedly returned it READ MORE :

5 View 5 Images Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53 5 View 5 Images Sheryl Wilkins was murdered by Levy (Image: Metropolitan Police/PA Wire)

‌



BTP said more women "may recognise [Levy] and have not yet reported what has happened to them".

British Transport Police said women who think Levy attacked them should report it, while the Met Police said it had investigated whether he had more victims, including further murders.

A source said on Wednesday that dozens of women had come forward to the Met while a number have also contacted the BTP over concerns they were targeted by Levy. It is unclear how many will prove to be Levy and officers are now in the process of investigating the reports in an effort to substantiate them.

‌



Levy was first convicted of sexually assaulting two women in 2018, which he was jailed for in 2021.

View 5 Images Levy is being probed over dozens of cases (Image: Metropolitan Police/PA Wire)

BTP has confirmed two officers have been moved to other roles due to "incompetence" in handling investigations into the assaults.

‌



Lisa Ramsarran, chief crown prosecutor for the CPS, said: "Our actions fell short of the standards that victims, families and the public are entitled to expect."

Deputy Assistant Commissioner, Kevin Southworth, said: “We know that this case has raised questions around the way Levy was handled and we have carefully reflected on the opportunities missed to prevent his violent offending. It highlighted that improvements needed to be made and we have not waited for the outcome of the IOPC’s report to implement change.

“As the Commissioner recently said, we are concerned by the fragility of the criminal justice system. As we have seen in Levy’s case, despite clear risk and rapid escalation, the courts defaulted to bail on two occasions. We now need to work together, with other judicial partners, to create and implement a plan of action which sees repeat offenders – like Levy – automatically placed on remand to protect the wider public.

‌



View 5 Images Moment Simon Levy was arrested (Image: Metropolitan Police/PA Wire)

The Met said in a statement on Wednesday: "Since the launch of the investigation, detectives have exhausted numerous lines of enquiry – including working with coroners – to identify whether Levy is responsible for any similar, unsolved incidents, including deaths.

"While they are yet to find anything they believe to be linked to Levy, they are urging anyone who believes they may be a victim of his to contact police.

Article continues below

"Reporting rape or sexual assault can be daunting and many victim-survivors will have concerns about speaking to the police."

Those with information about Levy who are yet to speak to police can do so via 101, quoting 4779/7AUG. People can also contact the incident room directly on 07751 700 330 or anonymously via Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Andy Burnham urges shops to pause disposable barbecue sales after Cobra heatwave meeting
News.content:
Andy Burnham urges shops to pause disposable barbecue sales after Cobra heatwave meeting

Prime Minister Andy Burnham convened ministers, officials and agencies as scorching temperatures persist across the country in the fifth heatwave of the summer

View 2 Images The PM convened ministers, officials and agencies as scorching temperatures persist across in the fifth heatwave of the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has urged all retailers to pause the sale of disposable barbecues in order to prevent more wildfires raging this summer.

‌



It came as the Prime Minister warned extreme heat conditions "could be with us for some weeks yet" after chairing an emergency Cobra meeting in response to the fifth heatwave this summer.

‌



Speaking on Wednesday evening, he said: "The big risk in terms of risk to the wider regions across the country is the risk of wildfires. What we are seeing is multiple serious incidents across the country.

‌



"Fire services by and large are supporting each other through mutual aid to deal with those incidents, but we are keeping a very close watching brief on them."

He added: "There is advice to the public here not to use disposable barbecues. We have today confirmed through the National Fire Chiefs Council that the framework restricting the retail sale of those disposable barbecues is being extended.

"Now I would ask all retailers big and small to adhere to that framework. Longer term we will look at whether a temporary ban in the summer months is justified." Most major UK supermarkets have already suspended sales of disposable barbecues in recent weeks in line with voluntary guidance from the NFCC.

‌



NHS must plan for heatwaves like winter crises to protect frail and vulnerable, Yvette Cooper says READ MORE :

View 2 Images Andy Burnham is looking at whether a temporary ban of disposable barbecue in the summer months is justified (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

The message followed Wednesday's Cobra meeting with the PM convening ministers, officials and agencies as scorching temperatures persist across the country in the fifth heatwave of the summer. They included representatives from the Environment Agency, the Met Office, and the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

Earlier this week, the Environment Agency said 71.3% of England is now experiencing "flash drought", following the country's driest July on record.

‌



Before the Cobra meeting, Mr Burnham also said people should not be using single-use grills "at this time" amid a "significant problem" of wildfires in the south, where a blaze hit protected heathland in the New Forest, Hampshire.

The Prime Minister said he was "certainly going to consider" a ban, adding: "I do believe we need to get the message out loud and clear. People should not be using those barbecues outside at this moment in time."

On Tuesday, a firefighters' union sounded the alarm, warning that the country is facing a "national emergency" amid the ongoing wildfire crisis. General secretary Steve Wright said: "Lives are being put at risk. This is only going to get worse unless we get a grip of it now and put in place a proper national strategy".

Article continues below

The Cobra meeting on Wednesday was the second this summer on heatwaves after one took place amid high temperatures in June.

The Met Office has said the UK is on course for its hottest summer on record. Rare amber "extreme heat" warnings have been issued by the forecaster for London and parts of the South East, East Midlands, East of England, West Midlands and South Yorkshire from 9am to midnight on Thursday.

News.title: Bus driver, 25, shot dead outside London pub named as devastated family pay tribute
News.content:
Bus driver, 25, shot dead outside London pub named as devastated family pay tribute

Auguste-Marie Bile-aka Amoa was described as an 'amazing person' and 'kind man' who died from being in 'the wrong place at the wrong time'

View 3 Images (Image: Metropolitan Police/PA Wire)

A 25-year-old bus driver who died after being shot outside a pub in Clapham, south London, on Monday has been named as Auguste-Marie Bile-aka Amoa.

‌



The victim died after he was attacked outside a venue by an assailant who was also hospitalised with a gunshot wound and was arrested on suspicion of murder, according to the force.

‌



The suspect remains in hospital under police guard.

‌



Paramedics raced to the area outside the Landor Pub in Clapham North, within three minutes of the incident, but despite their best efforts, the man was pronounced dead at the scene, a London Ambulance Service spokesperson said.

View 3 Images Bile-aka Amoa was shot outside a pub in Clapham on Monday (Image: Jonathan Brady/PA Wire)

Speaking near the scene, a fried of Amoa described him as a "cool guy" who was "in the wrong place at the wrong time."

‌



“I don’t have bad things to say about him.

“He’s a cool guy, like I said, bus driver, hard-working.

“It’s shocking because of who he is and his character.”

‌



The man, who also works as a bus driver, said the death is “going to hurt a lot of people”.

Another friend of the victim, who asked to remain anonymous, said he was a “great guy”, adding: “It’s been hectic, everyone’s very hot-headed right now, everyone’s obviously grieving and I feel extremely bad for his mother as well, she’s in bits.

“It hurts me as well.”

‌



Prior to his death, Amoa also worked as a volunteer at a local school, and helped to mentor young people, a staff member told The Metro.

View 3 Images Friends described the victim as a 'kind man' who was 'in the wrong place at the wrong time' (Image: Jonathan Brady/PA Wire)

"He was a lovely kid; he had played around the area when he was young and wanted to give something back.

‌



"He was a lovely guy, great with the kids who would look up to him."

Another family member told the publication: "He was an amazing person and a best friend. He loved driving, so bus driver was the perfect job. He was living his dream.

"I have a daughter, and he would buy her gifts and was such a kind man.

‌



"He loved music and dancing; he was just wonderful. I heard about the shooting yesterday, and I know he is in that area.

"I texted him and got nothing back, then I found out the news. I’m heartbroken.’

Detective chief inspector Claire Guiver, who is leading the investigation, said: “Our thoughts remain with Bile-aka’s family as they come to terms with this tragic incident.

‌



“We continue to appeal for anyone with information to come forward.

“If you were in the area at the time of the shooting, witnessed anything suspicious or have any CCTV, dashcam or doorbell footage that could assist our investigation, we urge you to get in touch.

“Any piece of information could prove vital in helping us piece together the full circumstances.”

Article continues below

It is understood the alleged gunman was hospitalised by injury inflicted by his own gun.

News.title: Schoolboy, 9, dead in tragic Birmingham crash as devastated brother pays touching tribute
News.content:
Schoolboy, 9, dead in tragic Birmingham crash as devastated brother pays touching tribute

A nine-year-old schoolboy who 'loved Pokémon and dinosaurs' has died following a serious collision between two cars in Kings Norton

View Image A schoolboy has died following a serious crash at the end of last month. (Image: BPM Media)

A nine-year-old boy has tragically dried after being involved in a serious car crash.

‌



The schoolboy, named only as Kyron, was critically injured during a major collision between two cars on Masshouse Lane in Kings Norton on July 28.

‌



Police, paramedics and an off-duty nurse rushed to save the boy's life and restarted his heart, before he was taken to hospital in critical condition.

‌



But after an intense fight to save his life, Kyrom passed away in hospital on Wednesday, West Midlands Police confirmed.

"His family have asked for privacy at this tragic time, and we would ask that you respect their wishes at this time," they said in a statement.

In a heartbreaking tribute shared on GoFundMe, Kyron's brother Darnel Gittens has shared a tribute to his "happy, loving and special" sibling who was "always full of dreams and determination."

‌



"Kyron was such a happy, loving and special child," his older brother wrote. "He loved Pokémon and dinosaurs, and he was always full of dreams and determination.

"He had so much he wanted to achieve in life and was the kind of person who wanted to turn his dreams into reality. As his big brother, I could never have asked for a better little brother."

He added: "The thought of having to say goodbye to him is something I never imagined I would have to face, and our family is completely heartbroken."

‌



Darnel said he started the GoFundMe page in order to give his little brother the "beautiful and dignified funeral he deserves."

"We want to give him the best possible farewell and celebrate the wonderful little boy that he was," he said.

"Any donation, no matter how big or small, would mean so much to our family during this incredibly painful time.

Article continues below

"If you’re unable to donate, sharing this fundraiser would also be greatly appreciated.

"Kyron, I love you so much, You will always be my special little brother, and you will never be forgotten."

You can donate to Kyron's GoFundMe page here.

News.title: Mum's anger at groomed daughter's death after she was wrongly charged with terrorism
News.content:
Mum's anger at groomed daughter's death after she was wrongly charged with terrorism

Emily Rudd reported Rhianan, 16, to the government's anti-terror scheme - only for her daughter to die after she was charged with terrorism, despite evidence she was a victim

The Schoolgirl Terrorist

A mother who reported her daughter to the authorities has described her anger, after the groomed schoolgirl was wrongly charged with terrorism offences and later died.

‌



Rhianan Rudd, 16, plotted to blow up a synagogue and scratched a swastika into her forehead after being radicalised by an American white supremacist. Despite evidence clearly showing autistic Rhianan was a victim, she became the youngest girl ever to be charged with terror offences in the UK - only for the case to be dropped.

‌



Five months later, in May 2022, she was found dead at a Nottinghamshire children's home.

‌



Rhianan's friends and mother Emily Carter have revealed in a new documentary what led up to one of Britain's most controversial youth counter-terrorism cases. In Channel 4's "The Schoolgirl Terrorist?" Emily told of her shock when she realised her daughter had become obsessed with far-right ideology.

View 4 Images Rhianan died after being wrongly charged (Image: BBC)

She said: "She came down and went: 'I've downloaded "How to Make a Bomb'''. She came over and sat on my lap like a two-year-old, put her arms around me and cried."

‌



Emily added: "That afternoon I actually went online to a form and referred her to Prevent." She wrote: "I need help with my 15-year-old daughter. She has a very unhealthy outlook on fascism - she also has massive dislikes for certain races and creeds…I have done my best to deter her from any such ideologies, but it seems to be falling on deaf ears."

View 4 Images Rhianan and Emily (Image: BBC)

It emerged this month that the number of people being flagged to the government's anti-terrorism scheme rocketed 39% in a year to a record high, with one in five reported over fear of extreme right-wing ideology.

‌



Prevent received 10,293 referrals in the 12 months to September 2025. Half were under 18.

Chesterfield Coroner's Court heard Christopher Cook, from Ohio, first contacted Rhianan when she was 14. She had previously told detectives that she had exchanged explicit photographs with the neo-Nazi, adding: "I did love him." Cook, 23, was jailed in the US in 2023 over a plot to attack power grids.

View 4 Images Christopher Cook, from Ohio, first contacted Rhianan when she was 14 (Image: BBC)

‌



Emily said: "He had groomed Rhianon to the point where she had sent him sexual videos of herself nude."

The FBI had passed this evidence to the British authorities many months before she was charged showing he had groomed, coerced and exploited her. Emily, who admits she has made mistakes that adversely affected her children, added: "They knew Rhianon was being sexually exploited but they kept on treating her like a terror suspect."

She added: "I know a lot the mistakes I made have affected my kids but when I'm telling someone else I can see what you're doing is wrong, listen to me and they did f*** all." Rhianon also had direct contact with American white supremacist Dax Mallaburn, who came to the UK to live with Emily, who was vulnerable having previously been in a violent relationship.

‌



View 4 Images Emily is angry at the way her daughter was treated (Image: PA)

Mallaburn has since fled the UK. Emily said her daughter had an apprenticeship lined up as a jockey and was making costumes for charity when she was found hanged.

She wept as she said: "She had so much to offer the world and she had a good heart."

‌



Rhianan, from Derbyshire, had gone from being a huge My Little Pony fan to obsessing about white supremacy. Rhianon's brother Brandon said: "It's clear that there were failings."

Rhianan was arrested in August 2020. The charges were eventually dropped in December 2021 after she told detectives that she had been coerced and groomed.

'The Schoolgirl Terrorist?' on Channel 4 on Thursday at 10pm.

Article continues below

For mental health support, call the Samaritans for free on 116 123, email them at jo@samaritans.org, or visit samaritans.org.

News.title: Watch: Solar eclipse seen over UK skies
News.content:
Millions of people across the UK have witnessed the most significant solar eclipse since 1999.

People gathered across the country on Wednesday to watch the spectacle, as more than 90% of the Sun was obscured by the Moon.

News.title: Students wait for A-level, T-level and BTec results
News.content:
Hundreds of thousands of students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive A-level, T-level and BTec results on Thursday morning.

Another record number of students are expected to find out they have secured a place at their first choice of university.

The cost of going to university has been in the spotlight this year, with mounting pressure on the government to reform student loan repayments and a renewed focus on technical education under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

But the chief executive of Universities UK, which represents more than 140 vice-chancellors, urged students to not "let politicians make your decision for you".

About 40% of 18-year-olds in England receive A-levels every summer.

Around 250,000 grades for vocational and technical qualifications are also expected to be released to students in England, including BTec National, Cambridge Technical, Cambridge Advanced National and T-level results.

AS-levels, which will count towards students' final A-level results next summer in Wales and Northern Ireland, will also be released.

This year, the pass rate for National 5, Higher and Advanced Higher exams in Scotland rose across the board.

And last year, the proportion of students getting top A-level results reached a record high, with 28.3% of all grades across England, Wales and Northern Ireland marked at A* or A.

News.title: Double killer and rapist given whole life sentence
News.content:
A serial sex attacker who had a "morbid fascination" with sex has been jailed for the rest of his life after he was found guilty of murdering two women and raping a third.

Simon Levy, 40, killed Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53, in March 2025 and 39-year-old Sheryl Wilkins five months later. Earlier that year, he raped a third woman in the same Tottenham car park where Wilkins was later found dead.

At the Old Bailey on Wednesday, Judge Mark Lucraft KC sentenced Levy to a whole life order, meaning he will never be released.

The sentence comes after police and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) apologised over a series of disastrous decisions that left him free to roam the streets.

When Levy carried out the attacks, he was on bail and being monitored by the Met.

The police watchdog is currently examining how he was managed over a four-year period, from his first conviction in September 2021 for sexual assault up to his final arrest in September 2025.

Following Wednesday's sentencing, Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said the handling of Levy's case was a "whole system failing".

News.title: Burnham urges shops not to sell disposable BBQs over wildfire risks
News.content:
Andy Burnham has urged shops to stop selling disposable barbecues amid increased wildfire risk driven by this summer's droughts.

The prime minister said he was urging "all retailers big and small" to adhere to voluntary guidance to suspend sales during extreme heat.

He added that in the "longer term" the government would look at potentially banning the single-use grills during summer months.

It comes after a potential ban was discussed at an emergency Cobra meeting on the government's response to record temperatures.

A number of large retailers and supermarkets have voluntarily stopped selling the devices under a framework, external agreed in 2023 between fire chiefs and the British Retail Consortium (BRC).

This says that retailers should suspend sales once an extreme heat event has been declared as imminent, or in response to "reasonable, evidence based" requests from local councils.

Earlier, Burnham told reporters single-use grills had been behind a number of recent blazes and people should not be using them "at this moment in time".

"We do want people to take the greatest possible care when they are out in the countryside, both in terms of cigarettes, but also those temporary barbecues that we know are causing risk of fires."

After the Cobra meeting, Burnham said: "We would say to retailers do not put disposable barbecues on sale at this moment in time."

Nearly three-quarters of England and all of Wales have been officially declared in drought, creating conditions rife for fire to spread.

The Met Office has issued a rare amber extreme heat warning for Thursday, with temperatures peaking in the mid-to-high 30s across the Midlands and south-east of England, and a high of 38C possible.

News.title: Jasper Carrott says family is 'so proud' of Lucy Davis after cancer diagnosis
News.content:
Actor and comedian Jasper Carrott has spoken about his pride and love for daughter Lucy Davis after she announced she has incurable breast cancer.

The actress, best known for playing receptionist Dawn Tinsley in BBC sitcom The Office, has received an outpouring of support since she revealed her diagnosis on Tuesday.

Carrott, who was one of the most familiar faces on British television over several decades, told BBC News: "This is a very difficult time for the whole family and we have been supporting her in every way possible since her diagnosis.

"We are so grateful for all the support we have had over this trying time and we are very hopeful for her future being what she wants it to be."

He added: "We are so proud of our daughter and love her so much. The way she has conducted herself through many traumatic health issues is a lesson to us all.

"We would request privacy for the coming months, but thanks once again for the love and concern shown by so many people."

Carrott, whose real name is Robert Davis, became a household name in the 1970s thanks to his stand-up comedy and novelty songs.

He has presented programmes such as Canned Carrott, Golden Balls and Carrott's Commercial Breakdown, and acted in comedy series such as The Detectives.

News.title: Eurovision Song Contest changes rules for countries at war
News.content:
Organisers of the Eurovision Song Contest have updated their rules to state that if a country involved in an armed conflict wins the competition, it will be ineligible to host it the following year.

The amendment was approved by the contest's governing body, following feedback from participating broadcasters after Eurovision 2026 in Vienna.

It states that winning countries will also be disqualified from hosting if a "sensitive geopolitical situation" affects the "security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region".

The update will be interpreted as a reaction to Israel's continued presence at the contest, amid criticism of its military actions in Gaza and the Middle East.

Last November, following a failed attempt to have Israel suspended, five broadcasters announced they were boycotting the competition - including Eurovision powerhouses Spain and Ireland.

Despite the protests, Israel's Noam Bettan ultimately took second place with his song Michelle.

It marked the second year in a row that Israel had taken the runners-up position - and some participating broadcasters have privately expressed safety concerns over the contest being staged in Jerusalem or Tel Aviv, should the country win in the future.

Although Israel will undoubtedly be seen as the target of the rule change, it will also affect Ukraine, which has been engaged in a protracted war since it was invaded by Russia in 2022.

Ukrainian group Kalush Orchestra went on to win Eurovision that same year, in a symbolic show of public support.

Following their victory, Eurovision organisers undertook a "full assessment and feasibility study" to decide whether the 2023 contest could proceed in Kyiv.

They ultimately decided the security risks were too great, and the UK stepped in to host the competition in Liverpool.

News.title: GB's Evans wins European gold in 100m breaststroke
News.content:
Great Britain's Angharad Evans won her first European Championship gold in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.

The 23-year-old comfortably finished first in a championship record time of one minute and 4.87 seconds, which was also a lifetime best and British record.

Having also broken the championship record in the semi-final, Evans claimed gold ahead of Ireland's Mona McSharry in second, while Italy's Benedetta Pilato took bronze.

Great Britain's Filip Nowacki, who made history for Jersey by claiming gold in the 200m breaststroke at the Commonwealth Games last month in Glasgow, was the fastest qualifier in the semi-final of the same event at the European Aquatics Championships.

The 18-year-old's time of 2:08.60 held off GB team-mate Greg Butler in the first semi-final, with the 25-year-old also progressing to the final.

GB's Amalie Smith picked up a silver medal in the 400m individual medley final, finishing 0.7secs behind Ireland's Ellen Walshe, with Poland's Justina Kozan claiming bronze.

The 16-year-old Smith, who won gold on Monday in the 4x200m freestyle relay, was also part of the part of the 4x100m freestyle relay team that finished fifth.

Another teenager, Italian Sara Curtis, also shone as she broke the women's 50m backstroke world record with a time of 26.63 seconds.

The 19-year-old bettered the world record set by Australia's Kaylee McKeown three years ago by 0.23secs in her semi-final.

News.title: First 100% British chocolate bar made since 1932
News.content:
A chocolate bar has been made using entirely British ingredients for the first time in nearly a century, with cocoa from not Brazil or Bali, but Berkshire.

Created at the University of Reading, it was named the Reading 100 Chocolate Bar to mark the university's 100th anniversary.

It is the first of its kind since 1932, when Rowntrees gifted a six-year-old Princess Elizabeth the only other bar of UK-grown chocolate ever made.

Food security master's student Maha Khan created the chocolate bar by harvesting, fermenting and processing the Reading-grown cocoa.

While the UK's chocolate market is worth Â£10.4bn, it is entirely reliant on imported cocoa.

Maha told the Today programme she made the bar to highlight the challenges facing the cocoa growing industry.

She said: "It is incredible that we can make 100% British chocolate â but in the context of climate change, pests and diseases, there are estimates that 30 to 40% is lost.

"And we've seen with these heatwaves, climate change, these problems and challenges are only going to get exacerbated."

News.title: New Forest wildfire continues as temperatures rise
News.content:
Firefighters on the fourth day of battling a wildfire in the New Forest are facing "challenging" weather conditions with temperatures set to rise again

The blaze began on Sunday 9 August when a van caught fire on the A31, with 23 drivers abandoning their vehicles as the fire took hold.

Hampshire & Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service (HIWFRS) said crews had implemented fire breaks and had a 'good hold' of the perimeter of the fire, while changing wind conditions were proving challenging.

National Highways said repairs to the A31 were not expected to be begin until Friday 14 August at the earliest.

News.title: Ministers push ahead with housing asylum seekers on ex-military sites
News.content:
Home Office minister Anna Turley has said the government is sticking with plans to accommodate asylum-seekers on former military bases despite protests from local residents.

She told the BBC the government's priority was to ensure asylum-seekers were looked after in a "secure" and "appropriate" place.

That included disused Ministry of Defence properties because they had on-site facilities and were "more contained," she added.

But campaigners in areas earmarked for asylum centres have said small communities with limited infrastructure would not be able to cope with large numbers of people.

There have been protests in Piddington, Oxfordshire, over plans to house more than 1,000 asylum seekers at a site near the village.

Mike Nixon, the vice-chairman of Piddington Parish Council, said there was a "huge amount of concern and worry" among residents and that an asylum centre would have a "dramatic effect" on the way they lived their lives.

The proposal has prompted Piddington to hold a symbolic independence referendum, asking its 400 or so residents if they want to remain part of the UK.

Nixon said: "We're still very frustrated. Andy Burnham did say that he's willing to listen, but we've had no formal contact. No consultation, nothing from the Home Office.

"We felt that the only way of making our views felt was to say 'well if we're not going to be listened to, what's the point of being a part of the country?'"

The government has promised to end the use of hotels for asylum seekers, announcing on Wednesday that a further 13 across England had been closed.

It plans to use former military sites instead with two already up and running - RAF Wethersfield in Essex, and Crowborough Training Camp in East Sussex.

In June, it announced proposals to open three more, including the site near Piddington.

The two other planned sites are a former RAF base in Barnham in Suffolk where there were protests last week and RAF Linton-on-Ouse in North Yorkshire where the area's Labour mayor said it was "simply the wrong place".

Defending the proposals on BBC Breakfast, Turley said the public wanted the government to end the use of hotels, pointing to how an "iconic" hotel in Blackpool, the Metropole, was no longer being used to accommodate asylum-seekers.

She said it sent "an important message" that the government wanted the hotel to be part of Blackpool's future.

"The priority is to ensure we look after asylum seekers in a secure place that is more appropriate and we limit the impact on communities."

Asked what she meant by secure, she said: "Examples we are looking at is former military bases and we have two up and running and possibly another three.

"They have have facilities on site and are more contained and it limits the impact on on communities.

"We are looking at other sites such as former industrial sites, student accommodation - accommodation that is more more appropriate than hotels."

News.title: I share concerns over Arday appointment, says Cambridge University head
News.content:
The vice-chancellor of the University of Cambridge has said she understands the concerns raised by the appointment of Jason Arday and shares them too.

In a letter to staff, Prof Deborah Prentice acknowledged the "anger and anxiety around this damaging and difficult case".

The university head also announced Cambridge's investigation would be independent and carried out by senior academics from within and beyond Cambridge and will begin "as soon as possible".

Arday resigned as a Cambridge professor of sociology of education last week amid allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements.

The 41-year-old - who became Cambridge's youngest ever black professor in 2023 - denies any plagiarism and said the recent furore had led to "an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack".

In a letter to university staff, Prof Deborah Prentice said: "I fully understand the concerns being raised across the University and well beyond it, regarding Jason Arday's appointment and I share them...

"We will now investigate the circumstances around his appointment by the faculty of education back in 2022 and his time here in Cambridge since his appointment nearly four years ago.

"That investigation, as you say, should be thorough and transparent, and will be carried out independently by senior academics from within and beyond Cambridge."
