The findings of the investigation, previously announced on Friday, will inform a review into the process for the appointment of senior academic roles, the university has said.

Prentice added "our staff of colour are highly valued, for their scholarship, their achievements, and the contributions they make" and said the case "should not be used to cast aspersions on their work or the legitimacy of their roles at Cambridge".

Cambridge had previously said allegations of plagiarism regarding Arday's thesis and some journal publications had been investigated by Liverpool John Moores University (LMJU) and the journals in question.

LJMU - which awarded his PhD in 2015 - had investigated the allegations that were made last year, and found he did not commit plagiarism.

In an interview with the Times, Arday defended himself by arguing that he had not received adequate supervision during his PhD given his autism and "learning disabilities".

The University of Cambridge said it had advised people to contact the relevant institution or pass on complaints.

But after Cambridge announced its own investigation, some academics pushed for the inquiry to be independent, questioning whether the university could adequately investigate its own processes.

It is not yet clear how the independent investigation will work or who will lead it. The university said it will look at the circumstances around his appointment by the faculty of education in 2022 and his time in Cambridge since his appointment.

Arday worked as a PE teacher before earning his doctorate at LMJU and going on to become an associate professor at Durham University and professor of sociology of education at the University of Glasgow.

Glasgow has also announced a review into Arday's previous academic post.

When he resigned from his post, Arday said he was not a "liar" and that his resignation "should not be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me."

News.title: Green councillor charged with assaults
News.content:
A Birmingham Green Party city councillor has been charged with attacking a member of the public, three police officers and a member of police staff.

Siobhan Harper-Nunes, 66, was arrested on suspicion of assault after police were called to the junction of Monument Road and Hagley Road in the city, at about 17:00 BST on Thursday.

Harper-Nunes, of Monument Road, was charged on Friday.

West Midlands Police said that she was arrested again at Monument Road on Wednesday morning on suspicion of harassment.

She remained in custody while inquiries continued, police said.

Harper-Nunes will appear at Birmingham Magistrates' Court on 10 September on the assault charges, the force said.

The councillor was elected in May to represent the Ladywood ward for the city council.

She previously stood as the Green Party's candidate for West Midlands mayor in the 2024 election.

The Birmingham Green Party has been approached for comment.

News.title: Man bled to death after being bitten by American XL Bully, court hears
News.content:
A man died from extreme blood loss after suffering "catastrophic injuries" when he was bitten on the leg by an American XL bully in his daughter-in-law's garden, a court has heard.

Keven Jones, 62, from Chester, who was in poor health, taking methadone and blood thinning medication, was staying at Chanel Fong's house at the time of the incident.

The incident took place before XL Bullies were added to the banned dog list in October 2023.

Fong, 33, denies being the owner of the dog, which the prosecution said was dangerously out of control at the time, and also denies an alternative charge of being the person in charge of a dog at the time of the attack.

Opening the case at Caernarfon Crown Court, prosecutor Mark Connor said it was a "sad and tragic case for everyone concerned" and told the jury they would be shown some "graphic images" of Jones' injuries during the trial.

He said it was not a case of whether the XL Bully, named Cookie, was a banned breed, but rather that the dog had been "dangerously out of control" and whether Fong was legally responsible for it, either as its owner or the person responsible for it at the time.

The court was told the dog was owned by Fong and her partner, Joshua Jones, the son of the victim, but that he was not present at the time of the attack.

Connor added that, in her police interview, Fong said on paper Cookie belonged to her partner.

He went on to describe how there were a number of dogs at the property on Holt Road in Wrexham, including Cookie and another XL Bully called Fire, who were in the back garden at the time.

Cookie's mother, an XL Bully called Rogue, was inside the property and was "in season" meaning she had been kept separate from the other dogs in the house.

News.title: Ann Widdecombe's loved ones gather for her funeral
News.content:
Police officers and sniffer dogs were in the grounds of the abbey ahead of the service, which lasted about 90 minutes.

The private requiem mass included a homily from the Rt Rev David Charlesworth, Abbot of Buckfast.

He said: "In the midst of the shock, clamour and sometimes unwarranted comment surrounding her death, our response is to pray for the repose of her soul, to give thanks for her fortitude, and offer Holy Mass in this Abbey Church which Ann called her safe haven."

A statement from the Abbey Church earlier said Widdecombe would be "missed and fondly remembered" and "many in our worshipping community knew her as a kind and warm character".

"Ann was a woman of profound faith, a faith which found expression in the public forum of politics," it said.

It added: "Ann was unafraid to express her unwavering convictions, formed through her Roman Catholic faith. She had a sharp intellect and was a dedicated public servant."

The order of service also included tributes paid by the Rev Roger Widdecombe, Widdecombe's nephew, and Sir Christian Sweeting, a close friend.

A public memorial for Widdecombe is due to be held later this year.

News.title: Victim of fatal Clapham shooting named
News.content:
A man who was shot dead in south-west London has been named by police as Auguste-Marie Bile-aka Amoa.

Officers and paramedics were called to Willington Road, Clapham, just before 22:00 BST on Monday following reports of gunshots near The Landor pub.

The 25-year-old, who worked as a bus driver, was pronounced dead at the scene, the Metropolitan Police said.

A 22-year-old man was later arrested on suspicion of murder after attending hospital with a gunshot wound on Tuesday. He remains in hospital under police guard.

Det Ch Insp Claire Guiver said her thoughts were with the victim's family as they "come to terms with this tragic incident".

News.title: Windermere signs to warn of algae poisoning risk
News.content:
Dozens of signs warning people about the dangers of algae poisoning are to be placed around England's largest lake.

About 40 notice boards alerting visitors to blue-green algae blooms, which can produce toxins that make humans ill and be fatal to pets, will be installed at Windermere, in the Lake District.

Blooms occur naturally but are more frequent during warm, dry weather and are exacerbated by nutrients from phosphate in pollutants such as sewage.

Funded by the Environment Agency (EA), a further 40 signs will be placed at other locations across Cumbria.

The Love Windermere Partnership, which includes organisations such as the EA, Lake District National Park Authority and United Utilities, said it was installing the permanent signs in response to requests for "clearer and more consistent public information".

As well as explaining what blue-green algae looks like, the notices will provide guidance on where to find current information about blooms and how to report suspected sightings using the Bloomin' Algae app, external.

The microscopic organisms can look like blue-green paint, scum or greenish-brown discolouration.

Gas prices on Wednesday hit their highest-ever price for this point in the year according to GasBuddy.

Patrick De Haan, the head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, reported in a post on X that gas prices have never gone above $4 per gallon after August 12 in any year.

On Wednesday morning, the average fuel price was just over $4 per gallon. The last time fuel cost nearly that much around mid-August was in 2022 when the national average gas price was $3.98 per gallon.

Gas prices have remained high for the majority of the year thanks to President Donald Trump’s ongoing war in Iran. Despite Trump's promises that fuel prices will "drop like a rock" once the war ends — and his frequent claims the the war has effectively ended and that Iran's military is destroyed while the U.S. controls the Strait of Hormuz — prices have continued to climb.

Approximately 20 percent of the oil used by the rest of the world travels through the Strait of Hormuz, which still appears to be under the control of Iran. The U.S. Navy is currently blockading the strait.

Gas prices over $4 per gallon at a station in Greenwood Village, Colorado. Gas prices have never risen beyond $4 per gallon by the August 12 mark in any previous year ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

Iran and Oman are currently negotiating an agreement to reopen the strait. An Iranian official explained on Saturday that Tehran is demanding the U.S. end its blockade, lift its sanctions, and pay war reparations before it agrees to open the strait.

Trump appeared hostile to Iran's terms, countering with his own demand that the nation pay "for all the people that they have killed and gravely wounded with their roadside bombs and many conflicts."

He reiterated his displeasure with Iran's conditions on Wednesday, claiming again on Truth Social that the U.S. has "total control over the Strait of Hormuz."

"I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT," he wrote. "Our Naval Blockade is being called, by everyone, 'A WALL OF STEEL,' and there is nothing Iran can do about it."

Trump's inability to end the war he started alongside Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has left him taking criticism even from some of his former advisers.

“The moment is extremely dangerous, and the Trump administration is showing uncertainty and incompetence,” Elliott Abrams, who worked for Trump during his first administration, told Politico.

An anonymous current U.S. official told the outlet that Trump "fundamentally misunderstands" Iran's leadership, and have wrongly "felt like they can just keep applying pain and Iran will crumble, but the regime is not going to crumble.”

With no end in sight, the Trump administration has released millions of barrels of reserve oil to try to avoid the blowback from increased fuel prices.

In March, Trump authorized the release of 182 million barrels of oil held in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to alleviate expected fuel shortages and price increases associated with the war. That release has brought the SPR to its lowest point since 1983, according to the Department of Energy.

The Independent has requested comment from the White House.

Newly-crowned European 400-metre champion Matthew Hudson-Smith joked he might run for “Mayor of Birmingham and Wolverhampton” after winning gold in his own backyard.

The Wolverhampton athlete, who grew up running on the same track at the Alexander Stadium, made it a hat-trick of career individual European titles, flying past a temporary stand named in his honour for the duration of the championships.

Hudson-Smith – the 2024 Olympic silver medallist over the same distance – was assigned lane nine, and got out to an early lead he never relinquished despite efforts to reel him in, holding off his challengers to cross the line in 44.17 seconds.

“Honestly, no, words (can’t) describe how much that meant to me,” Hudson-Smith told the BBC.

“I knew I was the best in the world. I knew that. On paper, I was a second faster than these guys.

“My coach said, once you seal the deal, make sure you do it. This is your home. Defend it.

“I knew it would take one hell of an effort to get past me. Every time someone beats me, I kind of end their career.

“I knew that for them to beat me, they would have to have a supernatural moment.

“Nobody is going to beat me on this track. This is my home. I have been here since I was nine. I know this track like the back of my hand.

“I have got my stand. Now I will go for Mayor of Birmingham and Wolverhampton. I’m going to keep asking, so all my boys are going to have a job at the end when I’m done, so let’s go. Vote for me, innit!”

The only dampener to the home favourite’s achievement was a third straight night where plenty of seats remained empty, even for the local’s final.

Muhammad Abdallah Kounta of France took silver in 44.40s and Jonas Phijffers of the Netherlands rounded out the podium in a national record 44.41s.

Myles Lewis-Skelly appeared to underline his commitment to Arsenal after setting aside transfer speculation to score in Wednesday’s 1-1 friendly draw with Italian club Como.

The 19-year-old has been linked with the Gunners’ Premier League rivals Chelsea and Manchester United amid uncertainty over his future.

Starting in midfield, he capitalised on an error from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez to slot the hosts ahead in the 33rd minute at Emirates Stadium.

Lewis-Skelly then made a heart sign to the crowd as he celebrated before tapping the club badge on his shirt on his way back to the centre circle.

The England international signed a five-year contract with Arsenal last summer but his long-term future has come under scrutiny since he fell behind Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie last term to become Mikel Arteta’s third choice left-back.

While he started only five Premier League games across the course of the campaign, he enjoyed an end-of-season resurgence in his natural role of centre midfield.

open image in gallery Bruno Guimaraes made his first appearance in an Arsenal shirt (John Walton/PA)

Arsenal, however, are well-stocked in that position after signing Bruno Guimaraes to join Declan Rice, captain Martin Odegaard and World Cup winners Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino.

Brazil international Guimaraes, who joined in a £75million deal from Newcastle on Saturday, was introduced at half-time against Como to make his Gunners debut, while Lewis-Skelly was replaced in the 62nd minute by Merino.

The Premier League champions were pegged back by Champions League-bound Como, who are managed by former Gunners midfielder Cesc Fabregas, when Martin Baturina equalised in the 43rd minute.

But Arsenal won the penalty shootout 4-3, with Guimaraes and fellow summer signing Christos Tzolis on target.

Noussair Mazraoui scored the decisive spot-kick as Manchester United beat Leeds 5-4 in a penalty shoot-out after their pre-season friendly at Dublin’s Croke Park finished 1-1.

There was the rare sight of Bruno Fernandes missing from the spot before it went to sudden death, but after James Justin’s effort struck the crossbar, Mazraoui finished the job.

Joshua Zirkzee had fired United in front in the 16th minute, set up by the excellent Bryan Mbeumo.

But Leeds drew level with the first real chance just before the half-hour mark, Brenden Aaronson applying the finishing touch after fine work from former United winger Daniel James.

open image in gallery Michael Carrick gave a number of youngsters an outing in Dublin (Niall Carson/PA)

Fernandes, on as a substitute, hit the crossbar late on but the 90 minutes ended in bizarre fashion after two young fans ran on to the pitch to take selfies with the United skipper.

When security did not immediately intervene, at least three others joined in and play did not restart before referee Neil Doyle blew for full time.

The match, the first game of association football at the home of the Gaelic Athletic Association since 2009, was played in front of a sell-out crowd of more than 80,000.

Lisandro Martinez, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford were among those watching on, not involved after only joining the training camp at the start of the week following the World Cup.

open image in gallery The match ended when a number of young fans ran onto the pitch (Niall Carson/PA)

But before the match Michael Carrick said he was holding the trio “in reserve” for Saturday’s friendly against former boss Ruben Amorim and AC Milan in Wroclaw, potentially Rashford’s first appearance in a United shirt since December 2024.

Mbeumo ran the first half. It was from his cross that Zirkzee brought a smart early save from Leeds’ record signing James Trafford.

The same pair quickly combined again for the opening goal. Mbeumo spun away from Jaka Bijol just inside the United half and charged down the left, drawing out Leeds new boy Tarik Muharemovic and slipping the ball through for an unmarked Zirkzee to finish first time.

Next, Mbeumo sent Diogo Dalot running through within two minutes of the goal, a vital interception from Muharemovic preventing a second goal, and then had United’s next clear chance himself.

open image in gallery Noussair Mazraoui scores the winning penalty (Niall Carson/PA)

He tried to find Patrick Dorgu but when Sebastiaan Bornauw cut out the pass, Mbeumo’s low shot was turned around the post by Trafford.

Leeds were level with 29 minutes gone. James drew two defenders as he ran at goal, then laid it off for Aaronson to do the rest.

Mbeumo could have had United back in front before the break but his curling shot, which picked up a deflection as it looped over Trafford, hit the underside of the crossbar and bounced clear.

After a flurry of half-time changes, including a debut for United’s new 18-year-old winger Tynan Thompson, Leeds should have gone ahead six minutes in when Joe Rodon’s low cross found Harry Wilson, but the summer signing’s shot was straight at Senne Lammens.

Fernandes was among six United players to join the fray on the hour and, having seen one strike ruled out for offside, he hit the crossbar with a curling effort five minutes from time before it went to penalties.

News.title: Man United v Leeds LIVE: Youri Tielemans scores in historic penalties win at Croke Park
News.content:
Carrick - the right man for right now

Manchester United required penalties to win the first ever club match at Dublin’s iconic Croke Park as they overcame Leeds United after a 1-1 stalemate.

Joshua Zirkzee, who appears to be putting himself in the shop window, opened the scoring for the Red Devils, slotting home after Bryan Mbeumo carved Leeds’ defence open from the right.

Leeds then equalised after former United man Dan James picked up a loose ball, threading Brenden Aaronson through to finish.

There were no goals after the break which forced penalties, and after new man Youri Tielemans scored and captain Bruno Fernandes shockingly went wide, James Justin missed the crucial penalty to allow Noussair Mazraoui to get the glory moment and fire in the winning spot-kick.

The infamous image of President Donald Trump staring directly into the sun during the 2017 solar eclipse has resurfaced - thanks to his own White House - nearly a decade later as another solar eclipse captivated viewers across the U.S. and U.K.

The White House shared the memorable image Wednesday afternoon as millions of people witnessed a once-in-a-generation solar eclipse, which occurs when the Moon passes in front of the sun, creating a bright ring of light around the lunar surface.

People wear solar filters or “eclipse glasses” when taking in the spectacle, since looking straight at the sun, especially during an eclipse, can damage the eyes. Looking at the sun is unsafe except during a brief period of totality, when the moon entirely blocks the sun’s light.

However, that didn’t stop Trump from staring directly at the sky during the August 21, 2017, eclipse.

Trump, who was watching the rare spectacle from the Blue Room Balcony at the White House, was pictured leaning back and looking up at the sky with his eyes uncovered and squinting.

open image in gallery The White House reshared an infamous image of President Donald Trump staring directly into the sun instead of using solar eclipse glasses

The president, then 71, reportedly gesticulated to a crowd of administration staffers gathered below the balcony and pointed to the sky. As he looked up, one of his White House aides then shouted, “Don’t look!” according to a White House pool report from the day.

The moment was immediately dragged on social media — and Trump continued to be trolled and made fun of for it for years to come, as the image resurfacing again in 2024 during another solar eclipse.

The White House’s resharing of the image Wednesday was immediately mocked yet again — while some even shamed the administration for sharing the image, as it may encourage others to participate in the dangerous activity.

“Unlike Trump, Do NOT look directly at the Sun during any phase of a solar eclipse without proper eye protection. Even a few seconds of unprotected viewing can cause solar retinopathy, permanent damage to the retina,” wrote liberal social media influencer Ed Krassenstein.

open image in gallery The image of Trump has been reshared for every solar eclipse since it was taken in 2017 ( AFP/Getty )

“This TWEET is irresponsible and dangerous,” he added.

“The president of the United States is promoting an act that can cause blindness as if it’s a troll. Think about who the intended audience is that might find this amusing. None of them recognize how humiliating this is for America,” another social media user noted.

Others found some humor in the messaging from the White House.

“The White House quote-tweeting NASA with a photo of him ignoring NASA is the whole second term in one image,” one X user wrote.

“Great point that he’s an idiot,” another X user chimed in.

Another social media user simply noted: “Generally not a good idea to try and blind your own supporters.”

News.title: Scots contend with clouds to catch glimpse of rare solar eclipse
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Scots across the country have come out in the hope of witnessing a once-in-a-generation solar eclipse – but many were left disappointed when it was covered by a blanket of cloud.

More than 90% of the sun was obscured by the Moon between about 6pm and 8.15pm on August 12, the most it has been blocked above UK skies since the total eclipse in 1999.

It is expected to be the fullest eclipse over local skies until 2081.

Crowds of skywatchers gathered at viewing events across Scotland on Wednesday evening eagerly awaiting the rare celestial phenomenon.

open image in gallery People gathering to watch the solar eclipse on Calton Hill, Edinburgh (Jane Barlow/PA) ( PA Wire )

People packed onto the summit of Calton Hill in Edinburgh, where the city’s astronomical society had organised a viewing event.

People formed a long queue at the observatory gates at the start of the evening hoping to collect a sought-after pair of eclipse glasses – but supplies ran out at about 6pm.

Others had brought kitchen colanders or home-made devices made from cereal boxes or sheets of paper for viewing the eclipse indirectly.

The eclipse began shortly after 6pm, with the “peak” extent of the sun’s coverage happening at slightly different times in different areas of the country.

It peaked in Inverness 7.03pm, when 90.74% of the sun was obscured, while in Edinburgh the peak came at 7.06pm, when 90.71% of the sun was covered.

open image in gallery Sophie Harju and Jack Nevin watched the eclipse with the aid of a colander and home-made pinhole camera (Nick Forbes/PA)

Some western areas of the country saw more than 92% coverage.

The skies above Edinburgh were covered by hazy clouds throughout the period of the eclipse, with the sun completely hidden behind thick cloud in the 15 minutes or so leading up to the peak.

People could be heard discussing the cloud cover, and whether there would be a gap in time for them to catch a glimpse of the phenomenon.

Cheers then broke out when the sun re-emerged shortly before 7pm, giving people a clear view of the partially-covered sun.

Sophie Harju, 26, and Jack Nevin, 27, both from Edinburgh, watched the eclipse using a homemade pinhole camera and a colander.

open image in gallery The solar eclipse as seen from Calton Hill, Edinburgh (Jane Barlow/PA) ( PA Wire )

Ms Harju, who works in the NHS, said she had not known what to expect, but that it had been “impressive”.

“It was a nice experience to see so many people out. But we maybe were expecting it to get a bit darker,” she said.

“It was a cool event to be part of and nice to see a little bit”.

She added: “This is the biggest Fringe show”.

Mr Nevin, who works in sustainability, said it was “cool” to see so many people come out to see it.

“People like the spectacle,” he said.

“They like when you can metric something, when you can say ‘this won’t happen again until this time’.

“I think people like to get together when there is something they can say is unique and novel”.

open image in gallery The solar eclipse as seen from Calton Hill, Edinburgh (Jane Barlow/PA) ( PA Wire )

David Ellis-Shea, who had come out to watch the eclipse with his wife and eight-month old daughter, said it was a “special moment”.

“We watched the Moon pass slowly in front of the sun, in between broken cloud,” the 34-year-old, who had been wearing eclipse glasses, said.

“We got very lucky to see it perfectly as it crossed over a sort of gap in the clouds. Almost perfect timing really.”

He added it had been important to bring his daughter to see it given the next eclipse of this scale is not due to happen until 2081.

“We were both reflecting that we probably won’t be here for that, but she may well be,” he said.

“And it was just a special moment to share with her, and hopefully she’ll be able to share that moment in the future with her family if she’s still around then, and remember the time she spent with us here.”

News.content:

Temperatures are expected to soar to 36C for parts of England, which will be hotter than Athens this week, as a fresh heatwave sweeps across the country.

Following persistent dry and hot weather, England and Wales are now in the fifth heatwave of the year. Parts of Britain will be hotter than the Greek tourist hot spot, which can expect highs of only 33C on Thursday.

The Met Office has predicted temperatures will climb “significantly” across the UK this week, increasing to between 32C and 34C on Wednesday.

open image in gallery Temperatures are set to hit the mid 30C on Thursday as a fifth heatwave hits the UK ( Met Office )

While weather maps currently show peaks of 35C across the South East and East Anglia, the Met Office said temperatures were likely to rise to 38C in parts of those regions on Thursday.

Deputy chief forecaster Mike Silverstone said the heatwave was expected to be fairly widespread across England and Wales.

“A fairly widespread heatwave is likely across large parts of England and Wales, with hot conditions developing in places,” he said.

open image in gallery The south and the Midlands are forecast to see temperatures of around 35C on Thursday ( Met Office )

“Humidity levels are also expected to increase through the week, which may make conditions feel more uncomfortable, particularly overnight.”

The UK has experienced a consistent North-South split in the weather across this summer, with Scotland and Northern Ireland having heavy spells of rain over the weekend.

Almost three-quarters of England and the whole of Wales are now in drought, prompting emergency services to warn of tinderbox conditions.

Temperatures are expected to reach 26C in Edinburgh on Thursday. Further south, temperatures will remain above 30C across England and Wales. The mercury is expected to peak at 32C in Darlington on Thursday.

Newcastle-upon-Tyne is forecast to experience 30C while Leeds and York experience scorching 33C heat.

open image in gallery All of England is under a heat health alert ( UKHSA/gov.uk )

Temperatures are set to remain hot on Friday with highs of 32C in London and 30C in Cambridge. But by Saturday most of England and Wales will experience cooler temperatures in the mid 20s.

All of England is under an amber heat health alert lasting until 9pm on Friday. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) warned of risks to the lives of the elderly and vulnerable people and significant effects on health and social care services.

Met Office five-day weather forecast

Today

Cloudy with outbreaks of rain in the northwest. Elsewhere, largely dry and sunny. Warm in Scotland and Northern Ireland, but very warm to hot across much of England and Wales, with locally very hot conditions in the west and southwest.

Tonight

Cloudier remains in the northwest with some patchy rain. Dry elsewhere with long clear spells. Warm to very warm across parts of central and southern areas.

Thursday

Very warm becoming hot or very hot across much of England and Wales. Chance of an isolated evening shower in the northeast. Heavier showers for Northern Ireland and Scotland later.

Outlook for Friday to Sunday

Mixed conditions, with sunny spells and mostly dry weather in the south. More cloud, showers and occasional rain in the north. Temperatures near normal, but warm in the southeast.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

News.title: Man Utd beat Leeds on penalties after selfie-seekers bring match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively but try explaining the half-hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only player the vast majority of crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breeched security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but, sadly, it shouldn’t have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold suggested they had taken a dim view.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle 1 Everton 3

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register, or login to an existing, telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.

When you see a + in the tracker it indicates how many other games start at that time.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, one exception is this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football will launch in the two weeks leading up to the start of the Premier League. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Chelsea set Enzo Fernandez 'deadline', Man Utd's £14m deal, Bradley Barcola hint
Sports.content:
The latest Arsenal, Liverpool, Man Utd transfer news and updates from around the Premier League as the window enters its final stretch ahead of the new season

Welcome to Mirror Football's live transfer blog for Wednesday, August 12. With around three weeks remaining, the window is entering its final stretch for Manchester United, Liverpool and more to get deals over the line.

Arsenal have been busy so far this summer, adding Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis but failing to land Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid. The Gunners remain linked to Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa, and versatile youngster Myles Lewis-Skelly is said to have been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United.

The Red Devils completed some fast deals to bring midfielders Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos to the club, but could still add another. They remain linked to Lewis Hall as Michael Carrick wants to strengthen his full-back options, and could also sign a striker if the opportunity arises.

Liverpool have confirmed the signing of Ronald Araujo to bolster Andoni Iraola's defence, having signed Spain star Victor Munoz earlier in the month. All eyes are on whether they can get a deal done for Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola before the deadline, however.

Join us for updates on those clubs and more as we take in the latest transfer news and rumours from the Premier League and Europe.

Sports.title: PSG continue to dominate Europe as Aston Villa narrowly beaten in UEFA Super Cup
Sports.content:
PSG continue to dominate Europe as Aston Villa narrowly beaten in UEFA Super Cup

PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN 2-1 ASTON VILLA: The season curtain-raiser between the Champions League holders and the UEFA Cup victors was narrowly won by Luis Enrique's side

View 2 Images Desire Doue scored the goal that won PSG the UEFA Super Cup (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista)

Paris Saint-Germain reaffirmed their status as the kings of Europe by beating their former boss, Unai Emery, and Aston Villa 2-1 to win the UEFA Super Cup in Austria.

‌



The UEFA Cup holders lined up below full strength with Emi Martinez, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins all missing following the World Cup. But even at full strength, Villa would have been up against it playing the team who destroyed some of Europe's elite on their way to winning a second successive Champions League title last season.

‌



Khvicha Kvaratskhelia broke the deadlock in style for the French giants 20 minutes in, chopping back onto his left foot from the right side of the box and whipping a ferocious effort past the helpless Marco Bizot. The goal was the Georgian winger's reward for an electric start to proceedings and left Villa with a mountain to climb.

‌



As impressive as PSG looked going forward, it was not all one way traffic; Villa's young guns up front, Brian Madjo and George Hemmings were in the thick of the action with Madjo going close twice in the team's pursuit of an equaliser.

View 2 Images Brian Madjo scored for Aston Villa before half-time to level proceedings (Image: Aston Villa FC)

‌



The 17-year-old forward finally got the goal his endeavour deserved on the stroke of half-time when he was picked out by John McGinn. Madjo lashed the ball into the roof of the net, sparking jubilant scenes.

Both teams had chances to nudge ahead as an entertaining second half wore on.

But it was Desire Doue who struck on the hour mark to break Aston Villa hearts, with the goal initially being chalked off for offside. Replays showed the Frenchman was well on, though, as PSG celebrated once more.

Please check back regularly for updates on this developing story.

Sports.title: Man Utd vs Leeds United friendly finishes early as multiple pitch invaders stop match
Sports.content:
Man Utd vs Leeds United friendly finishes early as multiple pitch invaders stop match

Manchester United's pre-season clash with Leeds United was brought to a premature close

View 2 Images A fan runs on the pitch which interrupts Manchester United's friendly with Leeds United. (Image: PA Wire)

Manchester United's game against Leeds United was brought to a premature halt as pitch invaders raced onto the pitch for selfies with some of the big-name stars. As the ball went out of play in the 89th minute following a Manchester United attack, five or six children raced onto the pitch to pose for pictures with some of their favourite players.

‌



Two made their way to the middle of the pitch for a picture with Youri Tielemans, who stopped what he was doing to pose for the young lads. The two kids then ran off the field of play, one with his hands aloft as he was cheered by the crowd, while a member of the security team gestured for them to leave the pitch.

‌



The security appeared to be booed by those in the ground, before cheers broke out as they safely made their way back into the stands. Their success prompted more kids to run onto the pitch, this time one United fan made a beeline for Bruno Fernandes, who also entertained the youngster, posing for a picture as more cheers broke out.

‌



Man Utd frustrated by Leeds as Bruno Fernandes reminder sent - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Jadon Sancho hits new low as club reject free transfer for Man Utd flop READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

More members of the security team made their way onto the pitch to remove the children, who had delayed play by two minutes, and referee Neil Doyle blew the whistle early to end the game.

Speaking on ITV commentary, Sam Matterface said: "Some young supporters have come running onto the pitch, which is not particularly helpful but they're being entertained by some of the senior players.

‌



"I don't think Daniel Farke is too happy about it. One has become two, now two has become three. They're all kids who are going up for selfies which is not great.

"Because the players are standing there and doing it, it's encouraging more to come on and do it. We've got a fourth one coming on which has caused a delay to proceedings and it makes a mockery of the security.

"A fifth one escapes a barrier and starts charging on, oh and a sixth. We'll have the whole lot on in a minute. Oh dear. It's a little bit of fun but it's not the greatest end to the match itself and the referee has decided to call a halt to proceedings to finish the game off and it'll be a penalty shootout at the end of the match.

‌



"Those incursions onto the pitch by some of the younger fans has just brought us to a premature close. We will have a penalty shootout for you very shortly."

View 2 Images A fan runs onto the pitch as he attempts to take a selfie with Manchester United's Youri Tielemans during the friendly with Leeds. (Image: PA Wire)

Joshua Zirkzee had given United the lead infront of a packed out Croke Park in the 16th minute after some great play from Bryan Mbeumo down the left.

‌



However, their lead lasted just 13 minutes with Brenden Aaronson equalising just before the half hour mark. Neither side was able to find a breakthrough and a penalty shootout was needed to separate the two teams.

The PA announcer had to interrupt the shootout to warn fans not to invade the pitch during the shootout as play would have to stop once more.

United ran out 5-4 winners with Harry Wilson and James Justin missing from the spot, with Fernandes missing for Carrick's side.

Sports.title: Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem
Sports.content:
Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem

Arsenal were knocked back by Aston Villa as they eyed Ezri Konsa earlier this summer but are ready to ramp up their interest despite the differences in valuation

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa is on Arsenal's radar this summer (Image: Getty)

Arsenal are ready to reignite their interest in Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa despite the two clubs being someway apart in their valuation of the player.

‌



Konsa has just enjoyed his best season to date, helping Villa win the Europa League and playing a key role in England's World Cup journey, which saw them make the semi-finals.

‌



The Gunners, who have wasted no time in bolstering their ranks following their Premier League success, saw a move for Konsa earlier this summer fail to take off. That owed to the fact they only wanted to pay £30m for the 28-year-old - whilst Villa wanted double that.

‌



Arsenal accept they will need to significantly improve their original offer if they are to sign Konsa, reports the BBC, but any move is also contingent on Villa being prepared to let their defender go, especially if their price isn't met.

Arsenal set to finally break record for transfer sale as bid submitted for Gabriel Martinelli READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta's desire to add a centre-half is likely motivated by William Saliba's injury, which he picked up whilst playing for France. His partnership with Gabriel is among Europe's best, but beyond them there is a lack of elite depth. Konsa's versatility is also seen as a major plus.

The England defender remains on holiday having been afforded an extended break due to his World Cup involvement. He was not in the Villa squad that played PSG in the UEFA Super Cup.

‌



Konsa has two years remaining on his contract at Villa Park and the Midlands side are eager to extend his deal. However his transfer value could drop off in the coming months if he does not agree fresh terms.

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa helped England reach the last four of the World Cup (Image: (Photo by Sarah Stier - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Unai Emery's side have already shown they are prepared to let their first-team stars leave, especially if they feel the price is right. Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea in a British record move whilst Youri Tielemans was allowed to join Manchester United. Lucas Digne has also returned to PSG.

Article continues below

Arsenal have successfully signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle this summer whilst Greek star Christos Tzolis has also been added. No major defensive additions have been made as of yet.

Sports.title: Man Utd chief gets blunt response to transfer approach - 'I'd tell him to go away'
Sports.content:
Man Utd chief gets blunt response to transfer approach - 'I'd tell him to go away'

Manchester United have been linked with Leicester City's Louis Page but Russell Martin has made it clear the teenager is not for sale

View 2 Images Man Utd are eyeing up a move for Leicester's Louis Page (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

Leicester boss Russell Martin admits he'd tell Manchester United chief Jason Wilcox "to go away" if he made attempts to sign teenager Louis Page.

‌



The 18-year-old was named the EFL Apprentice of the Year last season and is seen as one of the most exciting talents in the Football League - attracting attention from the Red Devils.

‌



Page would reportedly be keen on moving to Old Trafford if the opportunity arose, but Leicester are determined to keep hold of their academy graduate. The England U20 international has already made 21 senior appearances for the Foxes - including five starts last season. He played in their Carabao Cup win over Northampton on Saturday.

‌



Martin has been appointed as the Foxes new boss following their relegation to League One and he previously worked at Southampton with Wilcox, who is now the director of football at United. He admits, despite their history, he'd tell him to look elsewhere if they came looking for Page.

Michael Carrick told he must sign seven more players in urgent Man Utd transfer message READ MORE :

Youri Tielemans sends clear Marcus Rashford message to Michael Carrick after Man Utd reunion READ MORE :

He jokingly told Sky Sports: "Louis is a really fantastic young player. Obviously, I know the director of football at Manchester United very well after spending some time with Southampton. So we haven't actually spoken with Louis because he probably knows what I'd say to him and tell him to go away.

"But no, until something comes in that is really brilliant for the club, the player, and everyone is happy, then Louis stays, and he's in the squad. I'm really enjoying working with him. He's a fantastic young player."

‌



View 2 Images Leicester's teenage star recently signed a professional deal

Arsenal and Aston Villa have also shown an interest in Page. Leicester have already lost one of their leading young prospects this summer after seeing forward Jeremy Monga, 17, join Manchester City, and they will be loathed to see another leave the King Power Stadium.

Page signed professional terms with the Foxes in September last year, which means United would need to agree a transfer fee if they wanted to secure his services.

Article continues below

Leicester said after he penned his deal: "After joining us at Under-9s, Louis has progressed through our Academy ranks and developed within the LCFC pathway into one of the brightest talents in our system".

Sports.title: Man Utd edge Leeds in friendly shoot-out but Rashford does not feature
Sports.content:
Joshua Zirkzee and Brenden Aaronson scored as Manchester United and old foes Leeds played out an entertaining 1-1 friendly draw at the spiritual home of Irish sport in Dublin, before the concluding shoot-out was edged 5-4 by Michael Carrick's side.

On the eve of the new Premier League season, all the talk was about Marcus Rashford and his reintegration under Carrick, but the 82,000-strong crowd at Croke Park were not treated to a first glimpse of the forward in a Man Utd shirt for over 18 months.

Nor did they get to see a number of other high-profile stars until after the hour mark, Carrick instead choosing to give a raft of youngsters a proper run-out. His side improved immeasurably after the introduction of Bruno Fernandes and new signing Youri Tielemans, though, combining effectively to offer Matheus Cunha some pre-season shooting practice.

Image: Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin heads at goal

Fernandes himself was played through by Luke Shaw in the second period, much to the delight of the pro-United fanbase, who chanted 'Bruno, Bruno, Bruno' for large portions of the night, but his strike was flagged offside. He also struck the crossbar late on.

Of those senior regulars who did start, Bryan Mbeumo caught the eye, showing impressive intensity to tee-up Zirkzee for the game's opener. Dan James and Aaronson were Leeds' conspirators shortly after to turn home their first of five shots on target. Daniel Farke's side have scored a tidy 10 goals in five pre-season outings this summer.

The game was decided by a tight penalty shoot-out, where both sides missed, before Noussair Mazraoui stepped up to convert the winning spot-kick.

The key moments from Croke Park

16: GOAL! Joshua Zirkzee sweeps home a smart, low cross from Bryan Mbeumo.

29: GOAL! Dan James latches onto a punt from James Trafford and baits Ayden Heaven before feeding Brenden Aaronson to equalise.

46: SUBS! Leeds change the majority of their starting XI, with Harry Wilson, Dom Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor among those introduced.

60: SUBS! Michael Carrick sends on Bruno Fernandes, Youri Tielemans and Matheus Cunha.

80: RULED OUT! Fernandes' strike is chalked off after the offside flag is raised. He crashes an effort off the crossbar not long after.

PENALTIES! Wilson missed first for Leeds, but was reprieved when Fernandes also spurned his opportunity. James Justin's miss proved decisive as Noussair Mazraoui netted the winner.

What comes next?

Sports.title: Guimaraes makes bow and Lewis-Skelly scores as Arsenal held by Como
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes made his first appearance and Myles Lewis-Skelly scored amid speculation about his future as Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Como before winning 4-3 on penalties.

Guimaraes, signed for £75m from Newcastle on Saturday, was introduced at half-time in the pre-season friendly at the Emirates Stadium after Lewis-Skelly's opener had been cancelled out by Martin Baturina.

Lewis-Skelly's goal, stroked home after cutting out a poor pass from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez, came as he is linked with an Arsenal exit. He celebrated by making a heart gesture with his hands.

Guimaraes received a warm welcome with his introduction but Arsenal were unable to find a second-half winner before emerging victorious in the post-match penalty shoot-out in which Guimaraes and fellow new signing Christos Tzolis were among the scorers.

Image: Myles Lewis-Skelly celebrates his goal against Como

Mikel Arteta left out Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi despite their returns from World Cup duty this week, but there were first cameos of pre-season from Eberechi Eze, David Raya, Mikel Merino and Noni Madueke.

Sports.title: Atletico agree deal to sign Spurs captain Romero
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid have agreed a deal in principle with Tottenham to sign Cristian Romero.

The package is in the region of £34.2m (€40m) with add-ons. A 15 per cent sell-on clause is included.

Atletico have been long-term admirers of the Argentina international, and there was an expectation that Spurs would allow captain Romero to depart this summer if the right offer arrived.

The central defender was always believed to have preferred a move to Atletico, with Inter Milan and Spurs' north London rivals Arsenal among the other clubs to have been interested.

Romero's Spurs deal us due to run until the summer of 2029.

The 28-year-old was sent off twice last season during Spurs' Premier League relegation battle. He then missed the end of the campaign due to a knee injury.

Romero received criticism from supporters when he appeared to be set to watch his boyhood club Belgrano play River Plate in the Argentina Primera Division Apertura final instead of being at Tottenham's crucial last game against Everton. Romero did, though, attend the final game of the season, in which Spurs secured Premier League survival.

He has made 124 appearances for the club over five seasons, scoring 12 goals and being shown four red cards in the Premier League.

O'Hara: Time for Romero to move on

Speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, which will be available to listen to from midday on Thursday, ex-Spurs midfielder Jamie O'Hara said of Romero:

"He's a bit of a liability. When he plays, he costs us games, points and red cards.

"I just think his attitude towards the board and the way he was, I just think it's, 'All right, thank you, and we're going to move on'.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara calls for Tottenham to sell Romero

"We've finished 17th the last two seasons, and he's been involved. He was captain last season, and the way he acted at the end of the season, when he got injured and we all saw him crying, that wasn't for Tottenham; it was more for Argentina and his World Cup.

"And then he goes to Argentina on the last day of the season, and everyone's like, 'Where's Romero?' So that situation for me needs to be put to bed. I don't think we need any of that bad publicity around us.

"Get as much as we can for him; let him move on. We've got back up now with Van Hecke and Senesi, so thank you, see you later."

Spurs are set to make a loss on Romero, who joined from Atalanta for around £42m in the summer of 2021.

O'Hara said of Atletico's £34.2m deal for Romero: "The problem is there's a premium for English clubs, who will pay over the odds for people with European clubs inflating the fee.

"The problem is if you're going to go and sell him to Atletico Madrid, they haven't got the money.

"If we were selling him to Man United, we could probably get £60m-70 m for him. But the problem is if you sell a player to Europe, they just don't have the money that the Premier League clubs have, so you have to accept that it's going to be a lesser fee than what maybe you think you can get for him.

"He wants to go to Atletico Madrid. He just feels like an Atletico Madrid player. I just feel like you've just got to take that one on the chin and move on from it."

Sports.title: Birmingham Phoenix win battle to avoid Hundred wooden spoon vs MI London
Sports.content:
Birmingham Phoenix prevailed in the battle to avoid the wooden spoon in The Hundred women's competition as Ellyse Perry's composed half-century condemned MI London to a sixth defeat of a chastening campaign.

Both teams had managed a solitary victory heading into this fixture but a fifth-wicket stand of 66 between Perry (62no from 39) and Pakistan skipper Fatima Sana (36 from 32) ensured Phoenix halted a three-match losing streak to end with a consolation win and finish seventh in the table.

Set a modest target of 122, the hosts were wobbling at 48-4 after Jemima Spence and Davina Perrin fell in the powerplay and England duo Alice Capsey and Emma Lamb were dismissed cheaply, with Kirstie Gordon (2-20) making early inroads with her left-arm spin.

But Perry found a willing partner in Sana, who eventually fell to Nicola Carey when just seven runs were required, and the Aussie superstar secured the win with six balls to spare.

Sports.title: Sports fans watch on as Britain experiences fullest solar eclipse since 1999
Sports.content:
Cricket fans at Edgbaston were among sporting spectators given a stunning view of Wednesday evening's partial solar eclipse.

The sky took on an eerie darkness as the Moon obscured more than 90 per cent of the Sun, leaving only a slim crescent of light visible.

Spectators watching Birmingham Phoenix face MI London in The Hundred were able to take in the spectacle from the stands, with many wearing special glasses.

The eclipse was the fullest above British skies since the total eclipse in 1999.

Image: Many fans watched on at Edgbaston through special glasses

Other sporting events also took place against the unusual backdrop.

Floodlights were turned on in anticipation at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham.

Small groups, including Swedish athletes Erika Warff and Tilde Bjerager, gathered outside Alexander Stadium to observe the phenomenon, congregating on both sides of the terrace below the west stand.

Image: Floodlights at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham were also on in anticipation of the eclipse

Some were prepared with protective paper glasses while others watched through their phone cameras, although the rare occurrence was already obscured by clouds when it peaked at around 7.15pm.

In Salzburg, football fans attending the UEFA Super Cup between Aston Villa and European champions Paris St Germain also gazed skywards.

Image: Football fans watched on at the UEFA Super Cup match between PSG and Aston Villa in Salzburg
