Sports.title: European Super Cup: Paris Saint-Germain 2-1 Aston Villa – live
Sports.content:
now 17.08 EDT The presentation ceremony begins with referee Omar Artan and his assistants. Artan is delighted as his medal is draped around his neck, finally getting his flowers after being unacceptably messed around by the Trump-Infantino clown complex. The officials had a good game. Then Unai Emery, who is now four defeats from four appearances in the Super Cup, leads his team up for their silver medals. A big smile on his face too, which is lovely to see. He knows his team have acquitted themselves well tonight, even if they’re not going to get their hands on the silverware. Somali referee Omar Artan grateful for Super Cup chance after World Cup exclusion Read more Share

3m ago 17.04 EDT The matchwinner Désiré Doué speaks to BT Sport. “This is amazing … it is really difficult … before, you have to win the Champions League … we have done it for a second time so it is amazing for us … we are always hungry … we want more … we are really ambitious … we are a young team and we want to win everything this season again … of course [we can go even higher] … we always can improve!” Share

5m ago 17.03 EDT PSG become just the third team in history to win successive Super Cups, after AC Milan in 1989 and 1990 and Real Madrid in 2016 and 2017. They deserved their victory tonight, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Désiré Doué settling the game with a pair of peaches, but Aston Villa gave them a good test. When the dander is no longer up, Unai Emery will be content with how his side – very much a work in progress at the beginning of a big rebuild – competed against the best team in Europe. Villa also appear to have unearthed a couple of gems in 19-year-old midfielder George Hemmings and Brian Madjo, who at 17 has become the youngest-ever scorer in Super Cup history, having spent most of the first half flinging two-time European champion and Ecuador international Willian Pacho around like an old sock. Luxembourg will have a job convincing Madjo into playing a competitive international. Share

12m ago 16.55 EDT FULL TIME: PSG 2-1 Aston Villa The European champions retain the Super Cup! Share

13m ago 16.55 EDT 90 min +5: Hemmings, who has been impressive tonight, crosses from the left. Buendia flashes a header wide left. That should be that. View image in fullscreen Emiliano Buendia doing his best Platoon impression as he heads just wide. Photograph: Darko Bandić/AP Share Updated at 17.01 EDT

13m ago 16.54 EDT 90 min +4: Dembele overhits a defence-splitting pass down the inside right. Hakimi and Vitinha should be in on goal, but Bizot can claim. Share

15m ago 16.52 EDT 90 min +3: Cash tries to up the tempo, making a nuisance of himself down the right. But he only manages to run the ball out for a goal kick. A pained look on his face. Share

16m ago 16.52 EDT 90 min +2: Villa win the ball back and string together some careful passes of their own. Share

17m ago 16.51 EDT 90 min +1: PSG take the sting out of the game with some sterile hogging of the ball. Back and forth across the back line it goes. Share

18m ago 16.49 EDT 90 min: Dembele dribbles slowly down the middle and tries to steer a low curler into the bottom left. An easy snaffle for Bizot. There will be five additional minutes. Share

19m ago 16.49 EDT 88 min: Beraldo replaces PSG’s other goalscorer, Kvaratskhelia. Fans of Liverpool and Arsenal will note with interest that Bradley Barcola has been kept out of the action tonight. Here we go! View image in fullscreen Here come the siren emojis. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Share Updated at 16.50 EDT

22m ago 16.46 EDT 86 min: Mayulu comes on for Doué. Share

24m ago 16.44 EDT 84 min: Kvaratskhelia crosses from the left. Dembele blazes a wild volley deep into the stand behind. There’s another goal in this game all right. But for who? Share

25m ago 16.43 EDT 82 min: Dembele drives into space down the right. He cuts into the box and shoots. Blocked. The ball breaks to Kvaratskhelia on the right-hand edge of the six-yard box. Kvaratskhelia tries to dink over the keeper … unsuccessfully. Villa counter, with Abraham slipping Alysson into the box down the right. Alysson rolls an inviting ball through the six-yard box, but Abraham has made his run towards the near post, and can’t connect. Big chances at both ends! View image in fullscreen Tammy Abraham has a big chance to equalise for Villa. Photograph: Anna Szilágyi/EPA Share Updated at 16.47 EDT

27m ago 16.40 EDT 80 min: Buendia looks to have gifted Ruiz the ball, falling over weakly in midfield. But just as PSG prepare to counter en masse, the whistle goes for a generous free kick. Buendia gets up sheepishly. Share

28m ago 16.39 EDT 79 min: Kvaratskhelia again down the left. He tries to one-two his way into the box with Ruiz, but the scheme doesn’t come off. Villa then make a double change, taking off Torres and Gomes, both on yellows, and sending on Barkley and Mings. Share

31m ago 16.37 EDT 77 min: Kvaratskhelia probes down the left and rolls a cross into the box for Doué, who should get a shot away, but miscontrols with a heavy touch. Share

33m ago 16.35 EDT 75 min: Ruiz and Hernandez come on for Neves and Mendes. Share

33m ago 16.34 EDT 73 min: Alysson, Abraham and Bogarde come on for Kamara, Madjo and McGinn, who had just been booked for arguing with the linesman about nothing. Alysson is straight into the action, racing down the right and cutting back for Gomes, whose shot from the edge of the box is spectacularly blocked by the lunging Zaire-Emery. For a second there, a second Villa equaliser was on the cards! View image in fullscreen Alysson is causing all sorts of problems for PSG after coming on. Photograph: Darko Vojinović/AP Share Updated at 16.43 EDT

35m ago 16.32 EDT 71 min: Dembele strides down the left and feeds Mendes in the middle. Mendes pearls a shot straight at Bizot, who parries. The ball breaks to Kvaratskhelia, alone on the spot. Kvaratskhelia swings at fresh air. Nobody’s perfect. Share

38m ago 16.29 EDT 69 min: That aforementioned Hemmings chance has just been replayed. It was a huge one. Buendia had played him into space, just to the right of centre in the box. Either side of the keeper, and it was a goal. Straight at Safonov, ah well. View image in fullscreen George Hemmings holds off the challenge of Warren Zaire-Emery. Photograph: Jasmin Walter/UEFA/Getty Images Share Updated at 16.38 EDT

40m ago 16.27 EDT 67 min: A brief interlude, as Mendes goes down, his boot having come off. Then the referee gets overly fussy upon restarting the game with a drop ball. At least they didn’t crack open the drinks cart, because look at the time, it’s exactly Infantino o’clock. Share

42m ago 16.25 EDT 65 min: Mendes slaloms down the middle with Villa all over the shop. Maatsen intercepts a pass intended for Doué. Villa suddenly hanging on a wee bit. Share

43m ago 16.24 EDT 63 min: That was a lovely finish by Doué; shame he didn’t get to celebrate his goal in real time. But at least the correct decision was made. Hemmings tries to equalise immediately but his drive from the edge of the box is straight at Safonov. Then Gomes is booked for catching Doué from behind. It’s fair to say it’s all happening. Share

45m ago 16.22 EDT GOAL! PSG 2-1 Aston Villa (Doué 61) … but it’s a goal! VAR takes a long look, and turns out Cash, on the other flank, was playing Doué onside. View image in fullscreen Desire Doue beats the offside trap to put PSG back in front. Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty Images Share Updated at 16.28 EDT

47m ago 16.21 EDT 61 min: Dembele creams a pass down the right to release Doué, who enters the box, allows Bizot to come towards him, and from the right-hand corner of the six-yard box, whips around the keeper and in. The flag then pops up for offside. Share

48m ago 16.19 EDT 59 min: Hemmings snakes his way down the left and reaches the byline, before looping long towards the far stick. There’s nobody there for Villa, but Safonov isn’t sure of his bearings and, spinning around like a top, swipes out for a throw on the other flank. From that, McGinn crosses and Buendia heads harmlessly high and wide right. Share

51m ago 16.17 EDT 57 min: Zaire-Emery takes a whack from long range; Gomes blocks. Villa counter, Buendia barging into space down the middle. He should release Luxembourg’s Brian Madjo down the left, but hesitates and Hakimi is able to close down the passing route. Share

52m ago 16.15 EDT 55 min: Doué nicks the ball off Maatsen and enters the box from the right, but runs straight into his own man Hakimi. The pair confuse each other, and Villa clear. Share

54m ago 16.14 EDT 54 min: This scoreline shouldn’t be a surprise. Up to this point, Villa have had 11 attempts to PSG’s four. And that number stays at four, as Neves caresses a pass down the inside left for Dembele, who enters the box but loses control before he can shoot. That was a big chance. Share

55m ago 16.12 EDT 53 min: The Villa fans are in good voice. Their heroes hold their shape on the field, as PSG pass and probe. View image in fullscreen Photograph: Leonhard Simon/UEFA/Getty Images Share Updated at 16.16 EDT

1h ago 16.11 EDT 51 min: Torres is booked for clattering into the back of Doué. Share

1h ago 16.11 EDT 50 min: Buendia releases Madjo into space down the middle. Madjo drives upfield before rolling a pass to McGinn, who opens his body and curls towards the left. Safonov parries easily enough. Madjo continuing to announce himself on the big stage. “Gudden owend from Beggen in the Grand Duchy,” begins Andrew Drinkwater. “Please make sure you call him Luxembourg’s Brian Madjo: we know he’s gone and isn’t coming back, but at least until he gets his first competitive England call, he’s a Luxembourg international.” Share Updated at 16.18 EDT

1h ago 16.08 EDT 48 min: Doué drives in from the right and goes over upon entering the box. He wants a penalty, but there was no illegal contact from Hemmings, who simply stood his ground. Share

1h ago 16.07 EDT 47 min: A slow start to the second half, so here’s a reminder that, should things stay level, there’s no extra time. It’ll be straight to pens. “No way is that kid 17,” splutters a disbelieving Tim Smith. “That implies he’s still growing. Frightening. He just tossed Pacho about like a rag doll on a couple of occasions. Very nice finish.” Share

1h ago 16.06 EDT Villa get the second half started. PSG have made one change, sending on Dembélé for the debutant Akliouche. This is now the team that started the Champions League final for PSG, with one exception … and Fabián Ruiz is on the bench, ready to make it a full 11 out of 11. View image in fullscreen He’s on. Photograph: Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Shutterstock Share Updated at 16.11 EDT

1h ago 15.54 EDT Half-time postbag. “I thought about emailing something insightful about the actual game, but then thought well, why break the habit of a lifetime, this is the MBM after all, I’m on holiday and have been drinking whisky for four weeks solid, and DUNDEE UNITED ARE PLAYING CELTIC AT TANNADICE on Saturday in the Scottish League Cup, and there was a solar eclipse here tonight, the first since 1999, and it got slightly dark for a few minutes, so I think we all know what that means. John McGinn though, eh? If I could have one player at Tannadice, I think that’s who I’d choose. Come on Scotland United Villa!” – Simon McMahon “Five million euros for the winners, and four million for the losers. Not a lot of difference there. Maybe the Uefa coefficient points make up for it, but who understands them?” – Andrew Goudie “Here, where’s the hydration break? I need a cup of tea and there are surely one or two Villa defenders who need their twisted blood changed after Kvaratskhelia’s hi-jinks” – Justin Kavanagh “The last time I was in Salzburg I remember standing in a cobblestoned plaza enjoying a juicy sausage with oozing cheese filling (it tastes better than it sounds), a soft, buttery cinnamon pretzel and a cold glass of Stiegl. Good times” – Peter Oh Share

1h ago 15.50 EDT HALF TIME: PSG 1-1 Aston Villa That was great fun! Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is very much already a star; Brian Madjo is in danger of becoming one in short order. Share Updated at 15.55 EDT

1h ago 15.49 EDT 45 min +2: McGinn dances his way down the right, reaching the byline and cutting back, the ball somehow evading everyone in washed-out blue. PSG are suddenly all over the place! Share

1h ago 15.48 EDT 45 min +1: Madjo has been a handful since the get-go, and now he’s got his reward. Did he let his head drop after missing those good chances? Did he heck as like! And now at 17 he’s the youngest ever scorer in a Super Cup final, by a good couple of years. Patrick Kluivert, since you ask. Share

1h ago 15.47 EDT GOAL! PSG 1-1 Aston Villa (Madjo 45) Madjo’s got his goal now! Having missed three good chances, he ripples the net with number four! McGinn crosses from the right. Long. Madjo, wrestling with Pacho on the left-hand corner of the six-yard box, sticks out a leg and forcefully guides a shot into the top left from a tight angle! What a finish! A star in the making here! View image in fullscreen That’s brilliant from Brian Madjo! Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty Images Share Updated at 15.55 EDT

1h ago 15.46 EDT 44 min: Madjo is a prospect all right. Buendia dinks a cute reverse pass down the inside-left channel for the big young man, who enters the box, brushing off Pacho with slapstick disdain. He hammers a shot from a tight angle off the left-hand post and out for a corner. Somewhere in the multiverse, Madjo already has a hat-trick! Share

1h ago 15.44 EDT 43 min: McGinn is bowled over by Neves on the right. He takes the free kick himself. Madjo once again makes a nuisance of himself. The ball bounces around in the PSG six-yard box. Kamara, Torres and Lindelof fail to get into a position to nudge the ball goalward, and Safonov eventually claims amid a melee. Share

1h ago 15.43 EDT 41 min: Doué gifts possession to Buendia with a slack pass in midfield. Buendia advances on the PSG box and prepares to shoot, only for Kvaratskhelia to arrive and nick the ball away. The ball breaks left to Madjo, whose snapshot is deflected wide left. From the corner, the ball’s worked to McGinn on the right. McGinn crosses long, and Madjo heads wide from a couple of yards. He should have scored. But he looks a real presence. Share

1h ago 15.41 EDT 39 min: Kvaratskhelia wanders over to the right and is nearly sent skittering clear along the white line by Akliouche. The ball dribbles out of play, just in time from Villa’s perspective. Kvaratskhelia is utterly irrepressible. Share

1h ago 15.39 EDT 37 min: Hats off to Hemmings for cocking a snook to cynicism there. He’ll learn, of course. It’d have been the softest of penalties, mind. Share

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 6: Chelsea
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 3rd (NB: this is not necessarily Billy Munday’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 10th

Prospects

After a season of struggle and regression, with two head coaches and two spells under a caretaker, there is cautious optimism that this campaign will bring something like stability. Much of that optimism centres around the appointment of Xabi Alonso, an elite manager with something to prove. There is also an expectation that the young players brought in as part of BlueCo’s £1.8bn splurge in recent years are beginning to come into their best years. There is no European football to complicate the schedule and a return to the Champions League by finishing in the top four or five would suffice for now. More importance will be placed on the domestic cups after a season without trophies.

Alonso’s squad is more rounded than what Enzo Maresca or Liam Rosenior had at their disposal. Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers bring quality to positions where Chelsea were lacking it – at centre-back and out wide. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson – the “uncs” as Tosin Adarabioyo has called them – will contribute as much off the pitch as on it. The signing of Marco Palestra, a specialist wing-back, suggests Alonso wants to be tactically flexible. He has used a back four and a back three in pre-season.

What about Cole Palmer? For so much of his time at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea’s form has been tied to his. When he has struggled to be 100% fit, the team have suffered too. After being omitted from England’s World Cup squad, Palmer had a seven-week break and sought advice from a specialist on the groin injury that hampered him last season. “I got bored after six weeks,” Palmer said after returning for pre-season. “I was sat in Marbella thinking: ‘I want to go back in.’” With the prospect of linking up with Rogers and João Pedro, who has also had a good rest, Palmer has plenty of reasons to be excited.

Off-field picture

July ended with Chelsea being fined £10m and receiving a suspended transfer ban over multiple violations of transfer rules under the ownership of Roman Abramovich. An appeal from the club saved them from a six-point deduction. Chelsea were deemed compliant with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules for the three-year period ending in 2025 despite posting an English record £262.4m pre-tax loss for the 2024-25 season. They have not been cowed by failure to qualify for Europe and have spent over £300m on new signings. For the fourth year in a row, Chelsea look likely to start the season without a front-of-shirt sponsor.

Owner-fan relationship

Supporter protests against the ownership of Todd Boehly’s BlueCo have been a frequent sight on matchdays, including before May’s FA Cup final defeat by Manchester City. There have been reservations about the club’s youth-oriented transfer policy from the start and last season’s failings prompted the co-owner Behdad Eghbali to admit the need “to add more ready-made players” to the squad. Whether fans were expecting the arrivals of Welbeck and Henderson is another question. The introduction of a ticket ballot system for home games has also been unpopular with regular match-going supporters.

The manager

It was a bit of a coup for Chelsea to secure Alonso’s services this summer, especially given the Liverpool job was available. The Spaniard has a reputation to rebuild after his dream job at Real Madrid ended in the sack after six months. “I got a scar, now it is healed,” he said. Alonso’s record of developing young players, such as Florian Wirtz, at Bayer Leverkusen while simultaneously delivering silverware is a match made in heaven for the Chelsea hierarchy. One detail to note: Alonso has been appointed as manager, rather than head coach like his predecessors. He has also brought in Austin MacPhee, Aston Villa’s set-piece guru.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Chelsea broke the British transfer record to pry Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Chelsea went one better than Manchester City’s £116m signing of Elliot Anderson by bringing in Rogers, who had been linked with Arsenal, for a new British record fee of £117m. Although he started England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina on the right wing, Rogers has thrived for Aston Villa playing largely off the left and should slot in there nicely at Chelsea. The 24-year-old has proved himself in the Premier League and his best-buddy relationship with his former Manchester City youth teammate Palmer is a major plus. “I can see them linking really well,” Alonso said.

Stat attack

Has anyone checked Chelsea haven’t built a squad of Benjamin Buttons? The average age of their starting XI has decreased over the past three seasons when they were already the youngest team in Premier League history. You can see why they signed Henderson and Welbeck.

Set for a breakthrough

Robert Sánchez is still Chelsea’s No 1 but he may face serious competition this season from the 21-year-old Mike Penders. The goalkeeper, who was third-choice for Belgium at the World Cup, was signed from Genk in 2024 and spent last season on loan at Strasbourg in Ligue 1. The comparisons with Thibaut Courtois, who Chelsea signed from Genk at a similar age, are obvious. Like Courtois, Penders is 6ft 7in and therefore has a massive reach, but he also earns plaudits for his passing. Chances will come in cup competitions, but the clamour for Penders to be first choice might become hard to ignore.

World Cup impact

Enzo Fernández had a rollercoaster of a World Cup. Chelsea’s vice-captain popped up with crucial late goals for Argentina in the knockout stages, including a winning header against Egypt and the equaliser against England. But the abiding memory was his part in Argentina’s unsavoury approach in the final against Spain, where he received one yellow card for dissent and another for sending Pau Cubarsí flying. Real Madrid said in July they had “no intention” of pursuing a move that Fernández seemed to covet earlier this year when he said he would “love” to live in Madrid – comments that earned him a two-game ban under Rosenior. How about living in Manchester? City have been linked.

Sports.title: Xavi Hernández appointed head coach of the Netherlands on four-year contract
Sports.content:
Former Barcelona head coach Xavi Hernández has been appointed the new head coach of the Netherlands. The 46-year-old Spaniard has agreed a contract to lead the team through to the 2030 World Cup.

He replaces Ronald Koeman, who stepped down following the Netherlands’ last-32 defeat by Morocco at this summer’s World Cup.

Former Barcelona midfielder Xavi won the World Cup as a player with Spain in 2010 and also lifted the European Championship in 2008 and 2012. He guided Barça to the La Liga title in 2023 after beginning his managerial career with Qatari club Al Sadd.

“I consider it a tremendous honour to become head coach of the Dutch national team,” he said in a statement released by the Dutch Football Association (KNVB).

“As someone who received his training at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, among others, I feel a special connection to Dutch football. You could say that I am a bit of a son of Dutch football.”

Xavi’s appointment marks his first return to management since leaving Barcelona in 2024. He took over the Catalan club in November 2021, also succeeding Koeman, after making 767 appearances for the club.

“The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that also appeals to me enormously: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion, and conviction,” he said. “Of course, the most important goal is and always will be to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy. The potential for this is there, as well as a solid foundation to build upon.”

Former Liverpool head coach Arne Slot walked away from talks about replacing Koemanafter saying he wants to remain in club football. His link to the role did not get beyond an initial approach.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“At this stage in my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day, something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team,” Slot told Voetbal International. “And [it is] why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like.

“I have enormous respect for the national team and for the KNVB [Dutch Football Association] and can only be positive about the professional manner in which the talks proceeded that week. For now, I believe club football still has a lot to offer me.”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi has ‘quite a few doubts’ about football future after death of his father
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has hinted that the end of his career may be near after ­admitting to “quite a few doubts” about his football future following the death of his father.

Jorge Messi died last week at the age of 68 in Rosario, Argentina, after a long illness, with his health during this summer’s World Cup appearing to take a toll on Argentina’s 39-year-old captain.

In a tribute on Instagram on Wednesday, Messi wrote: “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you. I don’t know how ​to move forward. I only played football and now I have quite a few doubts about whether I’m going to keep doing it for much longer.

“You were by my side from the beginning; there was so little left until the end. Why couldn’t you hold on just a little longer so we could finish it together?”

Messi ​spent time with his ‌father after the tournament, where Argentina were beaten in the final by Spain, before rejoining his club side, Inter Miami, making his Major League Soccer return against Columbus at the start of this month.

Jorge had been a constant presence during his son’s career from his earliest days at Barcelona, with the World Cup the first time he had been absent from a major tournament. Messi revealed that his father, despite his deteriorating condition, had urged him to play for La Albiceleste in their ultimately unsuccessful attempt to defend their title.

“You always asked me to play in the last World Cup and a few days before it started was when you got worse,” he wrote. “It was the first time you weren’t going to be at a tournament … Every time a match ended, I would ‌wait and hope for your message. That’s when I realised how real the situation was.”

After tearfully celebrating the opening goal of his hat-trick against Algeria in the group stage, Messi had explained he was going through “a few difficult, complicated days” because of “something unrelated to football”. he said he ran out of energy in final.

“My legs couldn’t go on any more,” he wrote. “This time I tried to push myself beyond my ​physical limits, but I couldn’t. ​I never felt well … We weren’t champions, ​but you don’t know how much we enjoyed every match. Once again, you were ​right: I had to ‌be there and play ​it.”

Messi has earned 207 caps for Argentina since making his debut for his country in August 2005. He captained the side to World Cup glory in 2022, matching the achievement of Diego Maradona in 1986, though like Maradona he fell at the final hurdle when attempting to win back-to-back titles.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Messi did, though, break the record for total World Cup goals, with his strike against Egypt in the last 16 his 21st at the tournament and his 125th in all for Argentina. His World Cup tally was later surpassed by France’s Kylian Mbappé in the third-place playoff.

With his future uncertain it remains to be seen whether he will add to his remarkable CV of honours, which includes 10 La Liga titles, four Champions Leagues and eight Ballons d’Or in addition to that World Cup triumph in Qatar.

But he promised to honour his father’s memory through his own children: “I’m going to miss you so much, but you will always be present, especially in the upbringing of my children, because I will teach them and raise them the way you raised me.”

Sports.title: ‘It’s a nice hobby’: Manchester United’s Janina Leitzig on goalkeeping and gardening
Sports.content:
With some parts of England gearing up for a fifth heatwave of 2026 the new Manchester United goalkeeper Janina Leitzig, a keen gardener, is sympathetic to the precarious health of this reporter’s tomato plants. “You’re not used to so little rain, are you?” she observes. For the time being, after her summer move to Manchester, the former Germany youth international does not have a garden of her own but she reveals that, during her three-and-a-half-year spell at her former club Leicester, homegrown vegetables were her pride and joy.

“I love to do some gardening. Back home, everyone has their own vegetables and it’s just better, it tastes better,” she tells the Guardian. “Being away from home and away from family, of course you have your football friends, but still it can be quite lonely sometimes if you come home from training, so it was really nice to have a garden and to spend time outside. It’s not too much effort, it’s just a nice hobby.”

The 27-year-old got her outdoor fix with a spot of surfing in Cornwall this summer during the off-season, but now the serious business of pre-season is well under way. Her new club Manchester United are heading to La Manga for a training camp between 14 and 19 August, where the focus will have to be less on runner beans and more on running drills.

Leitzig, the former Bayern Munich and Hoffenheim keeper, was sitting down for an interview before it was known that the Spanish coach Eva Olid was to become United’s new manager, but explained why swapping Leicester for United was appealing to her. “It’s such a big club and it’s such a big honour to be here,” Leitzig says.

“I think, for every player, it’s really interesting if you have an offer from Manchester United. First of all, the team is so nice. The characters in here – you can tell it’s a really good and strong team. The training quality is really high. The building and the facilities [at Carrington] are really good; it’s really professional here. [When] the conversations were going on [with United], they just gave me a really good feeling.”

View image in fullscreen Janina Leitzig during a training session at Carrington. Photograph: Poppy Townson/MUFC/Getty Images

Leitzig has signed a contract with United until 2029, after the disappointment of relegation with Leicester last season, but says she has nothing but fond feelings about her former club, who she initially joined on loan in January 2023 before signing permanently that summer.

Looking back at what she learned in the East Midlands, she says: “It was such a special time for me. It was supposed to be only half a year and then it ended up being three-and-a-half. I think that says a lot about how much I liked it there. The people are great and the club is great.

“Obviously we had some tough times and unfortunately the relegation last season was really, really tough and it really hurt, because the club deserves to be in a better position, but I really hope that the girls will do well and I see them soon back in the WSL. It would be great if they could come back up quickly.”

During her time in England, Leitzig has observed an evolution in goalkeeping styles, and she is in a thoughtful mood when discussing what the future might look like for keepers, tactically. On the modern trend of keepers playing out from the back, she says: “To be fair, there was one phase where everyone wanted goalkeepers to play with the feet and I think it’s still really important, but I think there was a phase where it was too much. I think it was a bit overexaggerated at times, so I think it’s coming back now to be more about the basic stuff.

“Obviously you have to switch play and you have to be good with your feet under pressure, but I think the game is going to be more [about] trying to get the ball as quick as possible in the opposite half to then keep the pressure up there and not to try to take such a high risk. It’s going to be interesting.

“I think, because I’m German and Manuel Neuer [her idol] is German, I learned quite early to play with both feet and I was an outfield player initially, so I’m feeling confident about playing with the ball. But saving shots is the best part of goalkeeping.”

The USA keeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce played in 21 of United’s 22 matches in the Women’s Super League last season and Leitzig says they will enjoy working together and helping each other. “They [United] said it’s like a competition [to start in goal]. Obviously it’s really important to have strong goalkeepers, because you never know what happens in the season.

“I will just give my best, I’ll try to bring quality, and then it’s the manager’s decision to decide who’s going to play. But it’s really important that we are a good goalkeeper team, that we support each other and push each other because then everyone can get better.”

United, who finished fourth last season, will get the new WSL season under way on the opening night, at London City Lionesses on 4 September. Leizig concludes by looking ahead to that showdown and says, with fire in her eyes: “To have the first game of the season Friday evening, 7pm, floodlights, it’s just something you’re really excited for. Working in the pre-season you think: ‘When can the [games] finally start,’ so I’m really excited for that game.”

Sports.title: Barcelona make improved £51m bid for Rodri as Manchester City target Fernández
Sports.content:
Barcelona have made an improved bid to Manchester City of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri. This follows Barça’s initial offer of €45m that was rejected out of hand by City.

The Spanish club’s new offer – which may include add-ons – is close to City’s valuation for the 30-year-old who captained Spain to the World Cup and won the Ballon d’Or in 2024.

As the midfielder has declared a preference for Barcelona it seems it is inevitable he will leave. In preparation City are targeting Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández as a potential signing though the west London club’s valuation of around £120m may be too high.

Chelsea are understood to be intent on that price for the attacking midfielder so any transfer may include add-ons. Enzo Maresca is keen on Fernández after working with him for a season-and-a-half at Chelsea before his tenure ended in January.

The 25-year-old was a key member of Maresca’s team that finished fourth and won the Europa Conference in 2024-25 and the Fifa Club World Cup last summer.

If City were to sign Fernández, a World Cup winner with Argentina in 2022, another midfielder could be offloaded, with Tijjani Reijnders a possible candidate to depart.

As Rodri is intent on a move to Barcelona the arrival of Fernández, Chelsea’s captain, would add seniority and leadership to Maresca’s squad and a player whose combative style would offer an edge to City’s play.

City have so far recruited Elliott Anderson for £116m from Nottingham Forest and are close to the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi for around £85m from Lille.

Chelsea are thought to have enquired about Bournemouth’s Alex Scott as a replacement for Fernández should he leave.

City announced on Wednesday the signing of Gerónimo Rulli on a two-year deal following James Trafford’s move to Leeds. The Argentina goalkeeper was previously at the club in 2016-17.

The 34-year-old said: “My job now is to train hard, get to know the players and staff and do everything I can.”

Newly-promoted Hull have broken their transfer record to sign Senegal defender Nobel Mendy from Spanish side Rayo Vallecano. They also signed Australia international Lucas Herrington on Wednesday.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Tigers have not disclosed the fee for the 21-year-old Mendy but it exceeds the reported £20m they paid for Greece goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis last week.

Mendy, who has one international cap and previously played for Paris FC and Real Betis, has signed a five-year deal, with an option for a further 12 months.

He finished his only season with Rayo Vallecano with an appearance in May’s Conference League final loss to Crystal Palace.

“I have wanted to play in the Premier League since I was little, so it’s a great challenge to face and I am ready for it,” Mendy told Hull’s website.

Herrington, 18, became Australia’s youngest player to start a World Cup game for the Socceroos this summer, and arrived from MLS side Colorado Rapids on a five-year deal.

Sports.title: Championship angst: why the sense of rejuvenation in EFL is not universal
Sports.content:
A new season is supposed to be about renewed hope and optimism, a fresh campaign opening up a world of possibilities, a clean slate. But with the English Football League due to kick off on Friday night when Wolves host Blackburn in the Championship, the sense of rejuvenation is not universal.

The lineup of Championship teams this season is fearsome. Wolves and West Ham, hitherto established Premier League clubs, have dropped into the second tier. Others such as Burnley, Middlesbrough and Southampton anticipate a promotion push. So perhaps supporters of those who are not enjoying parachute payment riches and squads still packed with top-flight talent are wise to feel cautious. Some fear a long slog of a season to come.

Blackburn fans, for example, saw their side scrape to the safety of a 20th-place finish last season, therefore would be forgiven for tempering their expectations before the trip to Molineux. Tony Mowbray has been brought back to Ewood Park as an experienced guiding hand, but the 62-year-old has a huge task to avoid a relegation battle.

Fans believe the Rovers owners and the club’s head of football operations, Rudy Gestede, have sold Mowbray short on players heading into the season, particularly in midfield. The 34-year-old Sam Morsy – described by Mowbray as “a real man, a soldier” – has added steel to that area of the pitch with his free transfer, but after Moussa Baradji and Jayden Fevrier he is only the third addition at Blackburn this summer. Mowbray wants and needs more.

“I’m a bit greedy for good players,” he said. “I keep saying to Rudy: ‘I just want good players, doesn’t really matter where they come from, what age they are.’ I want to see personality on the pitch, players who are desperate to win.”

Blackburn edged past Burton 2-1 in the Carabao Cup first round last week, though they required late goals from Andri Gudjohnsen and Fevrier, who Mowbray believes can bring “magic” on the right wing after signing from Stockport.

View image in fullscreen Bolton Wanderers celebrated victory in the League One playoff final but a tricky season lies ahead. Photograph: Nigel French/PA

Down the road, there are two other Championship clubs feeling a similar sense of trepidation before the new campaign, and they meet at the Toughsheet Stadium on Saturday lunchtime, a game that could set the tone for their seasons. Bolton should still be on cloud nine; they finished last season with a 4-1 demolition of Stockport in the League One playoff final. Yet as the football world has witnessed this summer at York – where the manager, Stuart Maynard, was sacked and replaced by Scott Lindsey, despite winning the National League with 108 points – the afterglow of promotion can be short-lived. Reality bites quick.

And such is the chasm between the second and third tiers nowadays, the need for Steven Schumacher’s side to strengthen fast became paramount after that glorious day at Wembley. David Watson, Ben Davies, Akin Famewo, Luca Stephenson, Kyliane Dong and Gaizka Larrazabal have all arrived, but there is a feeling among the fanbase that a marquee addition is needed, especially in attack where they risk asking too much of the striker Sam Dalby. Schumacher’s admission last week that Bolton “can’t afford to waste money” rang alarm bells with the fanbase. There is not an embarrassment of riches in the pot but forward players must be signed.

“We know we’re short, especially at the top end of the pitch,” Schumacher said. “Our budget isn’t massive so we need to make sure we get the right players in, rather than just signing anybody to fill numbers. We need to try and consolidate this year, rebuild, get some more finances behind us, bring in a better squad that can keep us at this level, and then kick on.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Schumacher said that “this part of the journey is an exciting one” but it seems negativity among some fans has kicked in before a Championship ball has been kicked. A 1-0 defeat against Sheffield Wednesday in the Carabao Cup reinforced concerns around goalscoring, or the lack of it. Max Dean of Gent is coveted, but the striker is just 22 and his English football experience is limited to a short spell at MK Dons.

Preston will hope to take advantage of the uncertainty around Bolton on Saturday, but Paul Heckingbottom has endured his own problems in the transfer market this summer. A public spat with Ben Whiteman over the midfielder’s desire to join Wrexham left a cloud hanging above the club and saw the Lilywhites lose their club captain. Heckingbottom said Whiteman “crossed a line” and was frustrated by the saga.

Money has been spent at Deepdale this summer with Alfie Devine brought in from Tottenham for a fee in the region of £6m, while Callum Lang “feels like a new signing” according to Heckingbottom, having arrived in January for around £2m before getting injured. So the pressure is on Heckingbottom perhaps like never before. A run of just four wins from their final 20 matches of last season prompted a few fan murmurs of discontent towards the manager. With Preston almost investing £1.5m to install a modern hybrid pitch at Deepdale, the club expect better than last season’s 14th-place finish, but expectations can weigh heavy.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s ‘rock star’ plays the hits but will he find it hard to stay in Toon?
Sports.content:
IN A BLACK AND WHITE TOWN

As rallying cries for the dawn of a golden era go, “I am quite optimistic” is not “ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country”. It did not fit the “I think I am a special one” template set 22 years ago by Netflix’s latest documentary subject. Nor did Matthias Jaissle’s unveiling as Newcastle manager meet the pre-match billing of “fire” and “a rock star” that the club’s chief suit had promised the journalists in attendance. Though, considering the summer of tumult on Tyneside, it was a sensible path to take. Expectations among the Toon Army have certainly lowered since Geordies sunk Tin and donned tea-towel headdresses in celebration of Mike Ashley’s departure and the arrival of a consortium underpinned by the petrodollars of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. As it turned out, Lionel Messi neither ended up mowing the pitch nor selling the pies.

Depending on your perspective, that Newcastle have not yet been crowned Premier League and Bigger Cup champions is down to the servile football authorities bowing down to the hated red cartel or that day of wild celebration being one of false hope. The truth lies probably somewhere in between. A number of missteps pockmarked the last season of Eddie Howe’s reign. The “here we go” arrivals were nowhere near up to snuff. It should, though, be readily accepted that Newcastle enjoyed a good run under Howe, including an actual trophy and two rides on the Bigger Cup fun bus.

The Saudi connection has not paved St James’ Park with black gold (or Texas tea as the Beverly Hillbillies once had it). A pitfall of becoming the plaything of a top-level geopolitical operator is that those geopolitics may get in the way. Gulf states have a few things on their plates at the moment, and the interests of that investment fund stretch beyond a football club 3,000 miles from Riyadh. A new phase is entered; Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães are gone. Some might say the Saudis have lost interest, though Jaissle’s arrival from Al-Ahli, another club in the Pif portfolio, suggests hands are still on the tiller.

As for the new manager, the verdict was that he spoke very well at his premiere. “We were looking at each other with smiles and goosebumps,” he cooed, in describing his and his assistants’ first look at the stadium. Realism was offered in admitting a “vacuum” now those assets have been flogged off but there was no preview of the touchline histrionics various profiles have promised. Jaissle also followed the recent but now ingrained tradition of shaking each of his future interrogators’ hands. A classy gesture? A power move? Take your pick. Howe’s departure, and the loss of those big names, has returned Newcastle to the state of flux that was long their usual state of existence. How long can Jaissle’s calm and collected deportment last? How long can measured optimism sustain?

Sports.title: Cristian Romero takes big step towards Atletico Madrid transfer despite Tottenham agreeing fee with Serie A club
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid have agreed a deal in principle to sign Cristian Romero for a fee worth £34million, talkSPORT understands.

The Tottenham captain has long been tipped for a summer exit from north London, and Spurs had already agreed a fee with Napoli for the defender.



5 Romero's time at Spurs looks to be up Credit: Getty

The Serie A club were set to pay £34m for Romero, but were unable to agree terms with the player.

More recently, Romero was linked with a shock switch to Spurs' bitter rivals Arsenal, but any chance of this now looks to have ended.

Inter Milan also held talks earlier with him in the summer, but the Argentine is now set to get his dream move to Spain.



With a fee now agreed for him to join Atletico, Spurs will also retain a 15 per cent sell-on clause on any future transfer.

This comes after Romero agreed personal terms with LaLiga giants Atletico with the player to sign a four-year deal which has the option of a further year.



Romero is now set to join up with compatriot Diego Simeone at Atletico, in a move that will bring to an end his five-year stay at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

His expected £34m move also means that Spurs will make a loss on the £43million they paid Atalanta to sign Romero in 2021.



Tottenham's defensive overhaul

Spurs have signed centre-backs Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi this summer, with Micky van de Ven in positive talks over a new five-year deal.

This left Romero free to leave the club, despite penning a contract extension through to 2029 last August.

His imminent exit comes after he drew criticism from fans for his conduct and ill-discipline last season.

5 Romero now looks set to join Diego Simeone and his Argentine contingent at Atletico Madrid



Romero was sent off twice in 23 league appearances, and received ten yellow cards as Spurs narrowly avoided relegation.

The 2022 World Cup winner also became embroiled in a storm in May when it was reported that he was to miss Tottenham's crucial final game of the season in favour of a return to his homeland to watch formative club Belgrano.

With Spurs at risk of relegation and Romero getting wind of fan disgruntlement, he later changed his mind and instead was on hand to support his teammates in their quest for survival.

'Get rid of him'

As Romero closes in on a move away from north London, talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara had no qualms about Tottenham losing their captain.



Discussing the defender's links with Arsenal last week, the Sport Bar host and former Spurs player insisted the club would be better off without him, and claimed their new arrivals are better options.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, O'Hara said: “Get rid of him. I've heard there’s Arsenal chat about him - get rid of him.

5 The Argentine seeing red became a frustratingly familiar sight for Spurs fans in recent seasons Credit: Getty

“He was a liability for us last season. We’ve finished 17th in the last two seasons - he was the captain. He didn't want to be there on the last day. It was only because he got told that he had to come back that he ended up coming back.



“So get rid of him. We've got better players now. He's a liability.

“Van de Ven - make him captain. He's a player that you want in your side. You got Senesi, Van Hecke. Romero isn't even going to play.”

After two disappointing league campaigns, Tottenham have set about kickstarting a new era under Roberto De Zerbi this summer.

Spurs have splashed the cash in a bid to rebuild, spending £237m in total which includes twice breaking their club transfer record - first to sign Mateus Fernandes and then Sandro Tonali from West Ham and Newcastle respectively.

And O'Hara insisted there is no place for Romero in De Zerbi's new-look team, even after playing a central role in Argentina's run to the World Cup final.



5 Van Hecke looks set to fill Romero's boots after his £52million arrival from Brighton Credit: Getty

5 Romero helped Argentina through to a second consecutive World Cup final this summer, but his best form has often eluded him at Spurs Credit: Getty

Continuing to blast Romero, he added: “I'm happy to see the back of him.

"We need a new era under De Zerbi and it looks like he's putting a right good team together. We'll see what happens, but it looks like we've got a right good team and the players seem to like him.



“But Romero isn’t part of it. Get rid of him, get as much as we can."

Sports.title: Referee ends Manchester United vs Leeds friendly early
Sports.content:
Normal time of Manchester United's friendly against Leeds United was ended early after a string of pitch invaders disrupted the match.

The pre-season clash at Croke Park in Dublin was the first ever club football match at the iconic venue but was marred right at the end when multiple fans ran onto the pitch.



3 United's clash with Leeds was ended early after a pitch invasion by six supporters Credit: Getty

As the clock ticked down towards the 90th minute, a young supporter cleared the advertising hoardings.

Play was immediately stopped before five more fans invaded the pitch to take selfies with the players.

Whilst the TV cameras panned away from the incident, cheers could be heard from the crowd as each supporter entered the field.



Due to the disruption, referee Neil Doyle blew the final whistle before play restarted, without any added time indicated.

Meanwhile, it was announced on the PA system inside the stadium threatening to stop the match again if there were any more pitch invasions.



With the score level at 1-1, a penalty shootout followed once the pitch invaders had been removed.

United win on penalties

And the bragging rights belonged to Man United as they emerged victorious in the shootout, winning 5-4.



The decisive moment saw Noussair Mazraoui score the winning penalty after James Justin struck the crossbar with his effort.

United had appeared in control of the shootout after summer signing Harry Wilson was denied for Leeds by Dermot Mee.

However, an uncharacteristic miss from Bruno Fernandes as he sent his spot-kick wide resulted in sudden death efforts.

3 United beat Leeds on penalties to win the BOYLE Sports Cup Credit: Getty



The Red Devils captain's blushes were spared, though, after Youri Tielemans and Mazraoui found the target.

In doing so, United also get their hands on a piece of silverware by lifting the BOYLE Sports Cup.

Joshua Zirkzee had opened the scoring during the first half in the Irish capital.

His 16th minute strike made history as the first-ever club goal scored at Croke Park in its 142-year existence.



The match was the first association football match of any kind played at the 82,300-capacity stadium for 17 years.

Zirkzee's goal was cancelled out before half-time as Brenden Aaronson levelled for Leeds.

3 Zirkzee scored the first-ever club football goal at Croke Park Credit: Getty

When do United and Leeds play next?

United will now conclude their pre-season schedule against AC Milan on Saturday.



The two sides meet at the Wroclaw Stadium in Poland this weekend.

Michael Carrick's side then begin their Premier League campaign away to newly-promoted Hull City on August 22.

As for Leeds, they host Augsburg at Elland Road on Saturday before visiting Nottingham Forest on the opening weekend of the season.

Sports.title: Jeff Stelling predicts 2026/27 Premier League table and tips shock side for relegation
Sports.content:
Jeff Stelling has made his predictions for the 2026/27 Premier League season, including a surprise tip for relegation.

The new campaign gets underway next Friday (August 21) with champions Arsenal hosting newly promoted Coventry.



2 Mikel Arteta's Arsenal will be aiming to retain their Premier League title Credit: Getty

That's the first of 380 top-flight games to be played between then and May, with plenty of twists and turns inevitable.

But Stelling has already put his neck on the line by naming his picks for the title, European qualification and the drop.

Predicting the full Premier League table on talkSPORT, Stelling backed Arsenal to retain their title with Chelsea as runners-up, followed by Manchester City in third and Manchester United in fourth.



He placed Tottenham fifth – which has been enough for Champions League qualification in each of the last two campaigns – and Liverpool sixth, with Newcastle seventh and Aston Villa eighth.

Fulham to fall?

However, perhaps Stelling's most eye-catching prediction came at the bottom end of the table, where he felt Fulham would go down.



Joining Stelling on air, Peterborough chairman Darragh MacAnthony and former Villa striker Gabby Agbonlahor voiced their conerns over Fulham.

As well as Alvaro Arbeloa replacing Marco Silva as head coach, the Cottagers have lost key players this summer such as Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez.



Between them, Wilson and Jimenez accounted for more than a third of Fulham's Premier League goals last term.

"We called it as well, like two weeks, three weeks ago, didn't we, about Fulham," noted Agbonlahor. "We agreed that that's our team that could be under pressure..."

Stelling believes that Fulham could be in "big, big trouble" in the upcoming campaign.

2 Arbeloa is one of nine new Premier League managers for the start of the 2026/27 season Credit: Getty



The Cottagers' ostensible replacements for Wilson and Jimenez are youngsters Cesar Palacios and Gonzalo Garcia, both of whom have followed Arbeloa from Real Madrid.

And while striker Garcia scored six LaLiga goals at an average of just over one every 30 minutes last season, it remains to be seen how he'll fare in the more testing environment of the Premier League.

Fulham face a tough-looking opening fixture when they host West London rivals Chelsea on Monday, August 24.

Stelling positive about Sky Blues

While he tipped Fulham to be relegated alongside newly promoted Ipswich and Hull, Stelling joined MacAnthony in backing last term's Championship winners Coventry to survive – putting them 15th in his table.



Justifying his decision, he said: "Coventry...spent a lot of money – not on a huge number of players actually. They've chosen quality over quantity.

"Scored a lot of set-plays last season and that could be big for them again this season."

Sports.title: Roberto Martinez snubbed for Netherlands manager job with World Cup winner appointed
Sports.content:
Xavi has officially been announced as the new head coach of the Netherlands national team.

Roberto Martinez had looked the favourite to take the reins of the Dutch national team, who had been without a manager following Ronald Koeman's departure.

4 Xavi is making his return to the dugout Credit: Getty

Having stepped down as Portugal boss after their World Cup exit, Martinez was free to make an immediate return to management.

However, though the 53-year-old was interviewed for the Netherlands vacancy, he was ultimately turned down.

And in the Spaniard's place, the Netherlands have now appointed footballing legend and former Barcelona manager, Xavi.

The 46-year-old has not managed since his departure from the Camp Nou in 2024, where he spent three years in charge of his former club.

He guided Barca to LaLiga glory in the 2022/23 campaign, before leaving his role after a trophyless 2023/24 season.

As a player, Xavi played a key role in Spain's World Cup triumph in 2010, where they beat the Netherlands 1-0 in the final in Johannesburg, South Africa.

Before his three years as Barcelona boss, the legendary midfielder began his managerial career at Qatari team Al Sadd.

He spent 18 months in charge of the Middle Eastern outfit, winning seven trophies during this time.

'A great honour'

With Xavi the new Netherlands boss, he has become the first foreign manager of their national team in 48 years, after the Austrian Ernst Happel held the role between 1977 and 1978.

Reacting to his appointment, the Spain icon said: “It is a great honour to become head coach of the Netherlands national team.

4 Xavi enjoyed the greatest night of his international career against the Netherlands in 2010 Credit: Getty

4 Martinez stood down from his role as Portugal boss in the aftermath of their World Cup exit Credit: Getty

"As someone who was developed at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from, among others, Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, I feel a special connection to Dutch football.

"You could say I am, in a way, a son of Dutch football. Other great coaches, especially Louis van Gaal, under whom I made my debut at Barcelona, and Frank Rijkaard, have also played an important role in shaping me as both a player and as a coach.”

“The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that strongly appeals to me: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion and conviction.

“Of course, the main objective is always to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy watching.

"The potential is there, as well as a strong foundation to build on.

"I am looking forward to starting this challenge together with the players, the staff and everyone within the KNVB.”

4 Koeman recently stepped down after his second spell in charge of the Dutch national team Credit: Getty

Twist in the tale

Martinez had looked primed to take the Netherlands job, when reports in Holland claimed he was being lined up to succeed Koeman.

However, despite being interviewed for the role, with Dutch media revealing he spoke to he held talks with KNVB technical director Nigel de Jong over the position, his time away from international management will now continue.

The ex-Premier League manager spent six-and-a-half-years with Belgium, before his appointment as Portugal boss in 2023.

Despite his contract expiring at the end of July, Martinez immediately left his role after Portugal lost 1-0 to Spain in the last-16.

He was one of 17 managers that left their position as head coach either during the global tournament in North America, or after their run in the competition concluded.

The Netherlands were among those countries, with former boss Koeman calling time on his three-and-a-half-year spell in charge after Holland lost to Morocco on penalties in the round of 32 stage.

Martinez was among a number of high-profile names to miss out on the role, with Dutch publication De Telegraaf also reporting that Arne Slot, Erik ten Hag and Peter Bosz have passed up on the chance to take the reigns.

Sports.title: Wrexham sell defender to Championship rival
Sports.content:
Wrexham defender Lewis Brunt has completed a permanent move to Bolton Wanderers.

The centre-back has joined the newly-promoted Championship side on a four-year deal.

3 Brunt has joined Bolton from Wrexham on a four-year deal Credit: AFP

Brunt departs the Racecourse Ground after two seasons with the Red Dragons.

The 25-year-old was part of the side which won promotion from League One in 2024/25 following his arrival from Leicester City.

He is now set to face Wrexham in the second-tier this season as a result of joining the Trotters.

Brunt made 41 appearances for his former club, including nine in the Championship last term, scoring once.

Wrexham finished their first campaign at the level for 43 years in seventh place, missing out on the play-offs by two points.

They have since completed the permanent signings of goalkeeper Anthony Patterson, Crystal Palace full-back Danny Imray and former Preston North End captain Ben Whiteman ahead of the new season.

Brunt joins Bolton

Meanwhile, Bolton were promoted via the League One play-offs, ending their seven-year absence from the Championship.

Brunt becomes the club's eighth summer signing and their second from Wrexham.

He follows striker Ryan Hardie, who has arrived at the Toughsheet Community Stadium on a season-long loan.

Bolton have also added Luca Stephenson, Akin Famewo, Kyliane Dong, Gaizka Larrazabal, David Watson and Ben Davies to their ranks.

3 Brunt made 41 appearances for Wrexham and was part of their League One promotion-winning side Credit: PA

Speaking to the club's website, Brunt explained: "Stepping up from League One to the Championship is a big step up but if I can come into the building and try and help the lads and help the team then that's what I'll do.

"It’s going to be a challenge but it's one I'm sure the group, the staff, the team are all looking forward to and hopefully we can make it a positive season."

Bolton debut

Brunt was not involved in Wrexham's Carabao Cup defeat to Middlesbrough last Friday having been left out of the matchday squad.

He could now make his Bolton debut as early as this weekend with Steven Schumacher's side returning to league action at home to Lancashire rivals Preston on Saturday. The match is scheduled to kick-off at 12.30pm, live on talkSPORT.

Brunt will have to wait until December 11 to face his former club, though, as Wrexham make the trip to Bolton.

The two sides then meet in north Wales for the reverse fixture on New Year's Day.

Sports.title: Chelsea send Enzo Fernandez transfer ultimatum as Blues urged to keep £120m ‘dirty winner’
Sports.content:
Chelsea have set a deadline of 5pm this Friday for Manchester City to complete a deal for midfielder Enzo Fernandez, takSPORT understands.

The 25-year-old currently faces an uncertain future in west London, after he previously fuelled rumours of his exit, with the Citizens said to be keen on him poaching from their Premier League rivals.

4 Fernandez faces an uncertain future at Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

Fernandez heavily hinted at a move to Real Madrid towards the end of last season, only for the Spanish giants to shut this down in a statement saying they have 'no intention' of signing him.

A move to the Etihad could be appealing for the Argentine, which would offer him a reunion with former Blues boss Enzo Maresca.

Maresca left left Stamford Bridge on New Year's Day after a breakdown in relations at the club, a decision which Fernandez later appeared to criticise the Chelsea board over.

But with Fernandez boasting a huge £120million price tag, talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs recently revealed City could be deterred by this.

And they have now been handed an ultimatum, as Jacobs confirmed the Sky Blues have been told they until Friday to complete a deal.

Maresca's side are said to be keen on Argentina star, while Chelsea have made it clear his £120m asking price will only stay until Friday.

Following his involvement in the 2026 World Cup, where he helped Argentina to the final, Fernandez has since returned to Chelsea for pre-season training.

Chelsea told to keep Fernandez

The latest on Fernandez's future comes after former Manchester United goalkeeper Ben Foster urged Chelsea to do their utmost to keep him, calling him the 'dirty winner' that they need.

New Blues boss Xabi Alonso has previously voiced his desire to keep Fernandez, but his public comments hinting at a departure have understandably seen a number of fans turn against him.

His public image wasn't done any favours during the World Cup, when he drew the ire of England fans by mocking the Three Lions with a social media post playing their unofficial 'Wonderwall' anthem after Argentina's semi-final victory.

4 Fernandez made a pointed celebration after scoring against England in the World Cup semi-finals Credit: Getty

Despite Fernandez dividing opinion, former England stopper Foster has urged Chelsea to look past this and do their utmost to keep him.

With the midfielder playing a crucial role in Argentina's 2022 World Cup glory, Foster insisted he has the nasty streak needed to inspire a team to success.

Asked if he felt Chelsea would fare well without him on Tuesday's talkSPORT, the former goalkeeper said: “I still think they need to keep him. He's a little ferret, is what he is.

“But he's a winner. He's a horrible, dirty little winner that you want in your team. It's as simple as that."

Co-host Shebahn Aherne agreed that Fernandez's behaviour has long been divisive, pointing to his conduct at the World Cup.

The Blues star was sent off in Argentina's final defeat to Spain, as he received two yellow cards in quick succession, the second of which saw him send Pau Cubarsi flying into the air.

4 Xabi Alonso would benefit from having Fernandez among his midfield options, insists Foster Credit: Getty

Aherne said: “He was a disgrace. But listen, we've seen that with him before. We've seen his behaviour like that the whole time."

But Foster then insisted: “You want it in your team though.”

Fernandez has proven he brings more than just steely ruthlessness to a team during his time at Stamford Bridge.

Since joining Chelsea in January 2023 for a then British transfer record fee of £106m, the Argentina international has shown his ability to score goals from midfield, netting ten times in the Premier League last term.

End game for Fernandez?

While Foster insisted Fernandez' ruthless streak is what Chelsea need, it remains to be seen if the club will take the same view.

And while City have now been given a hard deadline over a deal for the World Cup winner, Jacobs recently revealed City could stop short of another nine-digit transfer.

4 Maresca and Fernandez shared a close bond while at Chelsea Credit: Getty

The Citizens have so far signed Elliot Anderson for £116m, while they are now in advanced talks with Lille over Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, for a fee expected to be in the region of £100m.

On Fernandez, Jacobs told talkSPORT earlier this week: "Chelsea's asking price was £120million. Now, maybe that's higher if you consider the fact that other deals, like Elliot Anderson - £116million.

"And Chelsea may argue that Enzo Fernandez should be more. He's a World Cup winner after all, and he was the vice-captain and captain at times of Chelsea.

“So Chelsea are calm about the situation, and they have every intent, if the window shuts, to try and get Enzo Fernandez on one extreme to sign the new deal.

“And yet, if their valuation is met, an exit is possible.

“We know that Enzo Fernandez has flirted with a move to Real Madrid. But if we take the public statement at face value, even with Rodri heading to Barcelona, the expectation is that Real won't move. You can never say never with Real, but they were put off by that asking price, according to my information.”

“So yes, City - specifically Enzo Maresca - do appreciate Enzo Fernandez. Are they going to find that budget questionable?

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold told why Real Madrid career is not over despite Denzel Dumfries transfer
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold told why Real Madrid career is not over despite Denzel Dumfries transfer

Denzel Dumfries' arrival doesn't mean the end of Trent Alexander Arnold's Real Madrid career.

That's the view of Real Madrid writer for The Athletic Mario Cortagena, who suggested the former Liverpool star will be Jose Mourinho's initial first choice at right-back this season.



2 Alexander-Arnold faces right-back competition from Dumfries (pictured) Credit: Getty

It's been a summer of changes at the Bernabeu, with Jose Mourinho returning as head coach and Dumfries among a raft of new signings.

But the Netherlands right-back won't automatically take Alexander-Arnold's place in the team, believes Cortagena.

Asked by talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor if he worries about Alexander-Arnold's game time for the upcoming season, he said: "Not really, because obviously he will have to deliver.



"But if you remember the first reports from early May, when Mourinho had spoken to the club to making plans about the transfer market, it was clear that he wanted a back-up for the right-back position, while for the left-back position, since the beginning, he wanted potentially a starter left-back.

"So, his starter right-back is expected to be Trent Alexander-Arnold. He's happy with him, but again, obviously this is football and Dumfries is understood to be a strong competitor for Trent and he should deliver to keep his spot in the starting line-up."



Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid from Liverpool last summer and made 30 appearances in all competitions in his first campaign with the 15-time European champions.

However, the 27-year-old has found it tough going adapting to his new club, enduring an injury-disrupted season which ended with him being left out of England's squad for the 2026 World Cup.



And with Mourinho's return to the Bernabeu and his reputation for defensive football, doubts had been raised over Alexander-Arnold's future in the Spanish capital.

Indeed, talkSPORT's Angelina Kelly said earlier this month that Liverpool should be open to re-signing their academy graduate, whose departure from Anfield sparked an angry reaction from fans.

"I’m not saying you’ve got to sign him immediately – let’s just explore this. Because Real Madrid have signed another right-back in Denzel Dumfries – that is not good news for Trent," she explained.

2 Alexander-Arnold has been reunited with Ibrahima Konate at Real Madrid Credit: Getty



Dumfries is one of six signings Real Madrid have made in the current transfer window.

Among them is Alexander-Arnold's former Liverpool defensive teammate Ibrahima Konate.

He's joined by another defender, Spain World Cup winner Marc Cucurella, who has moved from Chelsea.

And Bernardo Silva, Carlos Espi and Yan Diomande have also made the switch to the Bernabeu.



Real Madrid kick off the new LaLiga campaign away to Espanyol on Saturday, August 22.

Before then, they have two more pre-season friendlies against Deportivo A Coruna and Schalke.

Sports.title: ‘That is the problem’ – Arsenal and Man United scouts urged to wait for Brazilian talent
Sports.content:
‘That is the problem’ – Arsenal and Man United scouts urged to wait for Brazilian talent

Manchester United and Arsenal target Kaua Elias' movement is terrific - he can go a long way.

That is the verdict of European football expert Andy Brassell, who hailed the Shakhtar Donetsk striker for his start to the season.



3 Manchester United and Arsenal have been linked with a move for Shakhtar Donetsk sensation Kaua Elias Credit: Getty

Man United and Arsenal scouts were reportedly in attendance to watch Elias score a 'perfect' hat-trick at the start of last week.

Representatives for the two Premier League giants were in the stands for Shakhtar's first league game against Kudrivka.

Man United and Arsenal scouts watch summer target Kaua Elias

Elias, who is said to be valued at £30million and is also being eyed by Serie A giants AC Milan, took home the matchball in a 5-1 demolition.



However, Brassell wants to see the 20-year-old cut his teeth in the Champions League first instead of making the move this summer.

Shakhtar punched their ticket automatically for the league phase due to having the highest coefficient of all the clubs currently top of their domestic leagues from associations 11–55, since last season's finalists Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal have already qualified via their domestic league position.



It will be Elias' first appearance in the Champions League, having only arrived at Hirnyky (The Pitmen) in February 2025 from Fluminense.

On the small sample size involved, Brassell exclusively told talkSPORT: "I think that is the problem.



"Like when you look at Shakhtar's golden era - going back into the Mircea Lucescu years, when they were still in Donetsk.

"Then it was different because Shakhtar were a genuinely huge club that was on its way to becoming a European superpower, and I think you knew from the quality, not just the quality of the Ukrainian league then but the quality of their performances in the Champions League, that you were getting guys that were ready to go.

3 Shakhtar reached the semi-finals of last season's Conference League Credit: Getty

"So when you bought a Fernandinho, [or] Willian - they were like ready now," Brassell continued to talkSPORT.com.



"It's so hard to judge the level effectively of Ukrainian domestic football now through no fault of Ukraine's own or through no fault Shakhtar's obviously but that they are really living in extraordinary times and very difficult conditions and Shakhtar in a league with a lot of teams that would not be anywhere near the Premier League, if we were comparing it, which I'm always bit loathe to do.

"But the reality is Ukraine is not one of the top leagues at the moment, so I think you need to see them a little bit more in European competition.

"That's certainly the case with Kaua Elias.

"His movements terrific. I really like what I've seen of him, but again, I want to see him in the Champions League first."

Elias scored twice in five Europa League qualifying appearances last term, before finding the net the same number of times in Shakhtar's run to the Conference League semi-finals.



3 Shakhtar have been forced to play their European 'home' matches in Poland last season Credit: Getty

The Brazil Under-17 international registered an assist in the 3-1 home defeat to eventual tournament winners Crystal Palace in April.

But on Shakhtar's return to the Champions League, Brassell added: "To see them in that sort of context would be really important.

"Now bear in mind, say when Kevin came over to Fulham, and that's Fulham, not Arsenal or United, we'd seen some of him in European competition.



"So you knew that not only what he was able to do in there in the Ukrainian Premier League, but you'd seen a bit of him in Europe and you thought okay, this is something we can work with here.

"But this is Shakhtar's model now, to go out and buy really young players from Brazil, so a sort of accelerated version of the model that they used to do when they were in Donetsk and be able to inflate them into players that they can sell for three/four times that sort of money.

"Of course, they need to sell to survive, whereas before it was about selling to satisfy the dreams of those players and go and buy the next lot of players.

"It wasn't such a financial imperative because they were in a better financial position. The owner, Rinat Akhmetov, was in a better financial position.



"The country was in a better financial position, and the league was in a better financial position.

"But a great start to the season for Kaua; I think he can go a long way, but yeah, I need to see him in the Champions League first."
